findings.semantics: Keep original command names, argument truncation and numeric conversion, score request timing/debounce, Team Arena spectator handling, crosshair/attacker rules, each physical CLIENT console context and transport delivery. Native attacker data and remote snapshot data remain different input adapters, not different command behavior.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Wire/local identity mapping has a linear lookup on both directions and one lookup per admitted metadata actor.
findings.caller: prepare_frame -> stage_metadata calls frontend_remote_unified_source_actor for every world actor; model/effect/audio and component frame projection also call source_actor or wire_actor. Every mapping currently scans owner->identities, producing quadratic metadata admission as that retained list grows.
findings.replacement: Use the common qa_id_index keyed by validated wire slot/generation for wire-to-local metadata and qa_actor_index retained full-generation bindings for the local-to-wire reverse mapping; keep the list only for deterministic iteration and owned pooled payload retirement. The common actor index has one registry, so a foreign wire actor must first cross the explicit wire boundary.
findings.semantics: Validate wire registry at the existing boundary; preserve epoch resets, retained historical generations, zero/absent actor, distinct live versus historical lookup and the prohibition on resurrecting a retired wire identity. A retired actor may retain binding metadata without regaining live access.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof
findings.original_summary: Unified replica wire/local actor translation linearly walks a private identity list for each received actor and presentation lookup.

independent_review.conclusion: Wire/local identity mapping has a linear lookup on both directions and one lookup per admitted metadata actor.

source_evidence.evidence: Wire slot/generation lookup scans retained identities, including historical generations.
Reverse local actor lookup scans the same retained list.
Metadata staging invokes source_actor for every received actor.
Common actor index has remember/find_retained for full-generation historical identities.

independent_review.narrowing: An explicit wire/local namespace translator and retained historical generations are mandatory. Keep them; adopt common indexes for lookup. Do not call this list a duplicate authoritative entity table. Reserve historical-index capacity under actual retention bounds; no timing impact or sufficient fixed bound was measured here.

findings.summary: Remote Unified component source-slot and live-actor services privately scan the admitted actor-binding array on every lookup.
findings.caller: q3remote_component_open supplies source_actor/source_live to application_q3_scene_source; shared module collision, equipment and other host services reach those callbacks. weapon_presented also invokes source_live for the viewer.
findings.replacement: Build a common qa_actor_index for the admitted per-component actor bindings, including the reverse source-slot mapping, with qa_id_index for a wire slot key if the source range is not a direct physical index. Retain the ordered ABI actor view and owned flag; delete the lookup loops.
findings.semantics: Module physical slots and foreign borrowed actors remain distinct. Preserve full generation/registry equality, current versus acquired source context, baseline/frame ownership, actual actor liveness and the source-owned versus borrowed bit.
findings.verification: Per-frame module bindings use common keyed indexes while retaining full actor identity and current/baseline ownership. Native release uses the authoritative inverse slot mapping. Source correction, matching frozen-tree normal production build and seven existing core suites; no live game, audio, install, timing or whole-frame allocation proof.

findings.summary: Component player events are copied after received-ring delivery into a second deferred queue and consumed later during component draw.
findings.caller: frontend_unified_events_consume -> apply_presentation -> remote_unified_presentation.c:158 frontend_unified_components_player_event -> private qa_pool queue. Later frontend_unified_components_prepare_draw begins the component scene and drains the copied queue via application_q3_scene_consume before advance.
findings.replacement: Give each component scene one consumer cursor over the received ring, filtered by component owner/viewer and retaining the original record lease until that component is ready. Deliver from that cursor at the existing scene begin/consume/advance boundary and delete remote_component_event/event_records/events.
findings.semantics: Preserve received decode order, sequence deduplication, source-frame readiness, owner generation and recipient filtering, retired component discard, and the ordering of scene begin then consume then advance. This is an additional queue, not merely the final ring delivery callback.
findings.verification: Component player events are consumed by cursors over received ring records, retaining the original frame lease and readiness/decode order; the second private event queue is deleted. Source correction, matching frozen-tree normal production build and seven existing core suites; no live game, audio, install, timing or whole-frame allocation proof.
findings.original_summary: Remote Unified component player events are copied from the received event ring into a second pooled linked queue before scene delivery.

independent_review.conclusion: Component player events are copied after received-ring delivery into a second deferred queue and consumed later during component draw.

source_evidence.evidence: Presentation cursor delivers received records, then advances and retires the ring after both general cursors pass at 609-612.
Ring delivery calls frontend_unified_components_player_event and returns handled.
Takes a pool record, copies transformed event, appends target->events, records event_sequence.
After component begin, drains target->events through scene_consume; pool records are released before scene_advance.

independent_review.narrowing: This is the strongest actual extra internal event queue. It is not a Q3 reliable-command ABI history. Replace copied deferred storage with a component consumer cursor/retained original event lease, while retaining transformation/readiness/owner/recipient and begin-consume-advance ordering. Current event pool is load-sized; this finding does not assert per-event malloc.

findings.summary: The private component command window is mandatory Q3 module reliable history delivered as control metadata, not a duplicate of the received player-event ring; per-frame retention copies descriptors, not command payloads.
findings.caller: Reliable component control admission -> q3remote_component_state_read retains the newest 64 commands and rebuilds quoted command text/args; every q3remote_component_frame_read then frame_source_copy retains/copies the history again and supplies it to the scene module context.
findings.replacement: Admit the decoded component server commands once into an owner-scoped application_q3_command_cursor using the existing common ring/lease retention. Module readers borrow that cursor's retained command window; keep the typed incoming command vector only at the network boundary and an explicit frozen-frame cutoff where required.
findings.semantics: Preserve consecutive command_base/sequence, latest-64 backward reads, owner generation, frozen baseline/frame visibility, exact quoted text and args, acknowledgement/retirement and configstring fragment/map_restart/disconnect behavior. Independent module cursor instances are valid; duplicating command retention and frame copies is not required.
findings.verification: independent source/caller refutation; exclude original claim from work list
findings.original_summary: Remote Unified components keep and re-copy a private 64-command document/lease history beside the shared Q3 ring command cursor.

independent_review.conclusion: The private component command window is mandatory Q3 module reliable history delivered as control metadata, not a duplicate of the received player-event ring; per-frame retention copies descriptors, not command payloads.

source_evidence.evidence: Reliable component capture extracts consecutive new command arguments into qa_unified_component_q3 control metadata.
Admission validates command_base against previous command_sequence and keeps latest 64 commands.
command_retain retains document/lease, copies command/token descriptor structs and repairs argument pointer; it does not re-copy strings.
frame_source_copy freezes gamestate/revision/command_sequence and retains existing command descriptors for this frame.
Module scene requires command window bounded by snapshot.server_command_number and retains last 64 tokens, preserving older frame cutoff.
Suggested application command cursor stores text on a server/application ring with its own stream sequence and ACK subscription.

independent_review.narrowing: The command_text conversion for newly received controls is real ABI work; unchanged commands are shared through leases. The suggested application cursor is not currently a receiver component-control cursor and lacks frozen-frame token/document visibility as proposed. A common reliable-window primitive could unify implementations, but deleting this history as redundant or replacing it with the existing player-event cursor is not established. Refutation is of the high-severity duplicated-event-store claim, not proof all copies are optimal.

findings.summary: vid_restart duplicates native display projection and ignores the canonical r_mode selection.
findings.caller: vid_restart command -> qa_restart drain at frame.c:908 -> restart.c video_continue -> display_options -> qa_display_create. Normal bootstrap/publication instead calls frontend_shared_video_dimensions/settings.
findings.replacement: Use the existing frontend_shared_video_resolve/dimensions projection from one canonical settings reader for both initial/shared publication and restart.
findings.semantics: Preserve explicit cpu/gl backend choice, hidden replacement-window staging, fullscreen/swap/gamma and live dimensions fallback. A positive r_mode must select that mode, while custom dimensions apply only to r_mode -1.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Controller selection identity and selection-to-device matching are implemented separately with divergent equality rules.
findings.caller: Settings controller selection -> settings_devices input_prepare checks occupied seats and device identities; settings_menu checks current option; platform route rebind independently compares same selection.
findings.replacement: Expose one controller identity/equality and device matching primitive from the platform input owner and use it for route planning and menus.
findings.semantics: GUID comparison case/normalization, GUID ordinal, SERIAL serial and AUTO/NONE identity must be defined once; platform currently compares ordinal and whole GUID bytes even for serial while UI ignores serial ordinal and devices uses case folding. Preserve steal/rebind semantics without equating AUTO with every concrete device.
findings.verification: One controller selection equality/device matcher covers platform routing, settings and saves. Core checks GUID case/ordinal, exact serial and serial ordinal independence. No physical hotplug proof.

findings.summary: The shared audio actor binding still uses a growing private identity list and repeated actor/id scans on live sound and acoustic paths.
findings.caller: Builtin/protocol/native sound delivery -> frontend_audio_actor/retained_actor -> private linear audio_ids; acoustic listener trace -> source_acoustics trace -> reverse linear audio_ids scan. Rows are appended with realloc during first sound for an actor and only marked retired thereafter.
findings.replacement: Use the existing load-sized qa_actor_index for full-generation actor bindings and qa_id_index for retained audio-id reverse lookup, with one bounded common lifecycle owner.
findings.semantics: A freed actor generation may still own a queued sound; retain its sound identity until voices/event leases release it, never alias a reused actor slot, and keep round-retired ids unavailable to live listener traces.
findings.verification: Partial in da60a3cf: full-generation forward/history actor indexes and reverse uint64 bus index replace lookup scans. Aliases retire on successful round reset; same-round history and pool/index growth remain. Normal build and seven core suites passed; not whole-frame zero allocation or per-voice reclamation.

findings.summary: Selected foreign Q3 character frame outputs allocate and free heap storage for every rendered actor/frame instead of frame storage.
findings.caller: Native Q3 player-frame rendering enters frontend_native_character_begin, scans visible selected foreign appearances, allocates character_output, calls frontend_selected_character_build, captures material passes, and frontend_native_character_end frees all output/pass storage each frame.
findings.replacement: frontend->frame.storage via qa_arena_allocate for output rows and pass lists, as other frontend body/component frame adapters already use; retain the existing selected-character pose/content owner across frames.
findings.semantics: Keep q3n pose/animation rules, personal-model suppression, material pass order and output user leases alive until frame end; arena reset must follow all submitted consumers. Admission-only model loading is separate.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Unified Q1 and Q2 rerelease HUD/effects duplicate component retirement identity with growing private lists beside the shared received-event component store.
findings.caller: frontend_unified_presentation owner-event delivery calls frontend_unified_q2_rr_owner_retire; each new provider/generation allocates rr_retired and a provider copy. Every later RR HUD presentation tests retired by walking this private text list. The same event owner stores provider/content IDs and retirement in unified_component_owner. Q1 presentation/owner delivery similarly calls activation() and retains a q1_activation for every provider generation; retired rows remain until owner destruction.
findings.replacement: Use row->owner_provider_id/payload_owner_id and frontend_unified_events_component_current for lifetime qualification; retain only visual POI/bar/damage state locally, not a second lifetime identity table.
findings.semantics: Preserve exact provider generation, ordered retirement of all retained HUD records, objective center-print clearing and suppression of subsequent retired-owner events. Lifetime generations must not alias on refresh. Q1 retirement must also stop ambient/music and clear weapon/prompt/power/fog/finale state without affecting another provider generation.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: The selected Q3 effects adapter allocates mark scratch and grows reference-capture storage while producing live effects.
findings.caller: frontend_selected_effects_prepare -> prepare_primary -> q3n_local_submit/q3n_marks_submit -> capture_ref; impacts and bouncing fragments -> q3n_marks_impact -> selected marks callback. The callback callocs/frees mark fragments for each request and capture_ref reallocs when a live frame exceeds the previous high-water mark.
findings.replacement: Use the existing frontend frame qa_arena for reference capture and mark conversion scratch, as the Unified Q3 mark callback already does; keep genuine multi-frame local-entity/mark state in its persistent owner.
findings.semantics: Captured refs must remain alive until every view submits them. Fragment conversion preserves original ordering, point limits and uint32 boundary widths. This is effect-production allocation, not cold media admission.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Selected Q3 local-entity sounds generated during sampling bypass the common AUDIO record path and mutate the mixer directly.
findings.caller: prepare_primary builds a q3n_frame with effect_event=NULL and calls q3n_local_submit. A fragment bounce calls q3ne_sound -> effect_sound_output -> selected sound_output -> qa_audio_engine_play. qa_audio_engine_play calls play_impl directly and does not emit an application record. This is a newly generated bounce sound during local-entity advancement, not final delivery of an already committed AUDIO event.
findings.replacement: Emit the resolved qa_audio_event through frontend_audio_event/qa_application_audio_emit and let the common audio cursor apply it; keep one owner-qualified sound construction path.
findings.semantics: Keep the selected provider owner, fixed world origin, channel, asset/resource lifetime, audience and source millisecond timestamp. Bounce sounds occur once with original Q3 random/collision rules; avoid replaying already-delivered source effects.
findings.verification: One game-type conversion covers campaign and coop; selected Q3 sounds use common AUDIO delivery; per-frame resource policy refresh uses retained cvar modification counters. Source correction, matching frozen-tree normal production build and seven existing core suites; no live game, audio, install, timing or whole-frame allocation proof.

findings.summary: Unified presentation keeps private linked-list name caches and re-decodes inline model names on each model lookup.
findings.caller: Received-frame preparation -> frontend_unified_render_create -> model_read -> media_files/bank/model/skin. Unified Q2 effect pose sampling also calls media_model per sampled actor. Bank/model/skin hits linearly walk private lists although content/path arrive as qa_string_id; *N parsing runs before the cache lookup on every inline-model query.
findings.replacement: Index retained namespaces/bindings with qa_id_index keyed by content/path IDs and explicit request-policy discriminators. Decode inline-model slot once at admission and retain typed metadata; use existing scene resource/model owners for admission.
findings.semantics: Keep content namespaces, image-family policy, palette/translation requests, inline-world ownership and failed construction state distinct. Cold creation is legitimate; the gap is repeated private hit lookup and external-name decoding on the frame path.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Unified Q2 effects retain source-number-to-actor identity in a private growing alias array rather than the common actor binding index.
findings.caller: Decoded Unified Q2 temporary/muzzle records -> temporary_receive/muzzle_receive -> alias. Each new source number reallocs one private q2_alias; subsequent effect pose(number) linearly scans it before reading actor pose.
findings.replacement: Use a load-sized qa_actor_index per source namespace with reverse source binding and retained full-generation metadata; remove q2_alias and its private lookup/growth.
findings.semantics: Wire numbers remain an original Q2 boundary domain. Composed providers may reuse a wire slot; keep source qualification and exact actor generation needed by existing temporary effects without granting liveness to a released actor.
findings.verification: Unified numeric aliases have no reached consumer: typed temporary/muzzle records use full actors. Deleted alias realloc/store/scan, semantic source validation now requires its actual actor_pose. Legacy number callback preserved. Normal build/seven suites; no live effects claim.

findings.summary: Unified Q2 effect frame sampling repeatedly rescans the entire model frame and performs private quadratic actor deduplication.
findings.caller: frontend_unified_q2_lights -> sample_entities loops visual models. Every accepted row scans prior output rows for duplicate actor, then pose_actor starts another complete model scan and reconverts IDs until finding that actor. Temporary full_pose uses the same scan.
findings.replacement: Bind actor-to-model projection once per received frame with qa_actor_index, or project the row already being iterated. Use caller-owned qa_stamp_set for one-per-actor output admission; delete private scans.
findings.semantics: Preserve first-match model selection, activation/content/provider filtering, current-frame event gating, scale normalization, body-only fallback and full generation. Multiple model parts still produce one Q2 effect pose.
findings.verification: Shared historical renderer owns one common actor-to-first-model index; Q2 pose and sample callers use it with caller-local stamps. Original eligible sample ordering, generations and projection lifetimes checked. Matching normal build and seven suites; no live, timing or zero-allocation claim.

findings.summary: Unified Q3 prediction probes all possible entity slots to map an actor back to its Q3 number instead of reading a retained reverse binding.
findings.caller: q3_factory_prediction_prepare -> frontend_remote_unified_prediction_merged_q3 -> mapper.number for viewer, ground and jump-pad mapping. q3_prediction_number queries the snapshot for every slot below QA_Q3_ENTITY_WORLD until its full actor ID matches.
findings.replacement: Retain inverse snapshot bindings with qa_actor_index at snapshot admission and read that index for prediction merges.
findings.semantics: Mapping belongs to the historical snapshot/message, not merely the current live registry. Keep WORLD=1022/NONE=1023, exact generation, snapshot validity and restart lifetime semantics at the Q3 boundary.
findings.verification: Prediction and rendering read one snapshot-local retained actor index instead of scanning every source number. Historical registry/generation and WORLD/NONE boundaries retained. Source review, matching normal build and seven existing core suites passed; no live prediction or performance claim.

findings.summary: Unified prediction owns a separate clear-and-mark visitation bitmap beside qa_stamp_set.
findings.caller: Received frame -> scene_prepare clears pending_used for each old pending actor, then tests/sets a bool per collision actor to reject duplicate bodies. Storage is load-sized but marking/reset logic is private.
findings.replacement: One caller-owned load-sized qa_stamp_set begun for each scene_prepare transaction; use qa_stamp_set_mark for duplicate admission and delete pending_used.
findings.semantics: Reject two body rows for the same canonical slot after full source/generation conversion. Preserve pending rows and transactional validation; use common epoch wrap semantics.
findings.verification: Navigation SCC and Unified prediction use caller-owned qa_stamp_set. DFS order/cluster numbering and post-conversion duplicate admission are source-preserved. Cold mark storage grows from byte/bool to uint32; no speed claim. Matching normal build and seven core suites passed; no live or performance claim.

findings.summary: Unified Q3 projectile axes and Q2 tracker particles reimplement common direction, perpendicular and rotation math.
findings.caller: Unified Q3 ballistic_draw -> ballistic_axis -> private perpendicular plus sinf/cosf rotation for projectile refs. Shared Q2 tracker trails compute atan2/hypot and derive forward/up with their own trig sequence.
findings.replacement: Use qa_vec_perpendicular/qa_vec_rotate_around and qa_vec_angles/qa_angle_vectors, adding an explicit arithmetic rule for original tracker radians or float math if required, then delete local formulas.
findings.semantics: Do not substitute blindly: private perpendicular picks Z on equal-component ties while the common primitive picks the first minimum. Make roll/base orientation and original float/double/radian rounding explicit in the one primitive. Zero direction falls back to Z; particle spacing, oscillation and RNG remain original effect rules.
findings.verification: Q3 projectile perpendicular/rotation and Q2 tracker direction use common explicit original-source arithmetic policies. Original first-minimum ties, matrix rotation and float-before-wrap correct prior port arithmetic. Stationary fallback, effect count/spacing and RNG remain unchanged. Matching normal production build and seven core suites; no live or performance claim.

findings.summary: Model transform construction from origin and angles is copied in separate Unified world and Q1 static adapters.
findings.caller: unified_scene_visuals builds model transforms inline using identity, qa_angle_axis, origin and scale. Unified Q1 static/beam submission uses its own transform helper with the same identity/axis/origin projection.
findings.replacement: One model-transform-from-origin/angles primitive beside qa_model_transform_identity accepting angle math rule and explicit scale; callers retain only game-specific input selection.
findings.semantics: Keep matrix orientation, QA_ANGLE_FLOAT_MATH arithmetic, origin order and default scale. Differing animation and model rules stay separate.
findings.verification: Seven local and remote model-transform callers use the common constructor with explicit angle math and uniform scale. Two helpers and four inline builders deleted. Existing model suite verifies handedness, scale-before-translation and cardinal yaw for all angle rules. Prebuilt beam placement is untouched. Source/build/core only.

findings.summary: Unified Q1 and Q2 lightstyle retention and latest-event merging are private copies of a shared lightstyle capability.
findings.caller: Decoded style records write char* patterns and event-sequence arrays in Q1 groups/Q2 banks. Each world_input builds its own 256-entry seen/sequence scratch and selects the latest provider pattern with the same walk before sampling.
findings.replacement: Use qa_lightstyles for interned retained patterns and one common provider-style merge with per-style sequence metadata; extend the shared owner once for ordered composition instead of two private implementations.
findings.semantics: Multiple provider instances are valid. Preserve latest event sequence, tie order, defaults, retirement and original scale/rate through frontend_legacy_lightstyle_sample. qa_lightstyles lacks per-style sequence metadata today; add it once rather than discard ordering.
findings.verification: Source callers migrated and replaced paths deleted; matching normal production build and seven core suites passed. No live or performance claim.

findings.summary: Q3 SystemInfo propagation hand-parses the shared info-string format and duplicates case-folded key comparison.
findings.caller: frontend_source_effect receives SYSTEM_INFO -> frontend_source_system_info -> private strchr key/value loop and equal_ascii exclusions -> common cvar writes.
findings.replacement: Use borrowed-span qa_info_next and common case-folded info/key comparison; delete the local parser and equal_ascii. External-name-to-cvar writes remain at the protocol boundary.
findings.semantics: Keep pair order and duplicate application, optional leading separator, empty-key skip, case-folded download/timing exclusions, unchanged-timescale behavior, borrowed lifetime and frame-arena termination for cvar values.
findings.verification: Source callers migrated and replaced paths deleted; matching normal production build and seven core suites passed. No live or performance claim.

findings.summary: Per-frame live resource refresh compares retained cvar text and float words instead of canonical modification counters.
findings.caller: qa_frontend_step maintenance -> frontend_shared_resource_policy_live_sync -> live_recipe_changed each frame. Handles already exist, but every policy row compares string/number against a separately copied value.
findings.replacement: Retain handle modification_count on successful policy apply; early-out unchanged rows by integer revision and compare effective policy only on change. Delete per-frame text-based detection.
findings.semantics: Preserve i=3/4 nonzero equivalence and model-use/distance updates that intentionally avoid reopening assets. Equivalent effective rewrites may increment cvar revisions without requiring reconstruction. Revisions are explicit counters, not content fingerprints.
findings.verification: One game-type conversion covers campaign and coop; selected Q3 sounds use common AUDIO delivery; per-frame resource policy refresh uses retained cvar modification counters. Source correction, matching frozen-tree normal production build and seven existing core suites; no live game, audio, install, timing or whole-frame allocation proof.

findings.summary: Scene namespace and scene inventory duplicate replacement-model graph traversal and alias/cycle checking.
findings.caller: Namespace capture/import -> model_rows -> model_nodes builds a BFS queue. Inventory capture builds the same BFS queue in nodes before visiting node sources; both grow one pointer at a time and scan for aliases/cycles.
findings.replacement: One scene-model replacement graph iterator with caller storage and callbacks, used by namespace and inventory consumers; keep payload projection in each consumer.
findings.semantics: Preserve breadth-first namespace ordinals, root observation rules, child order, cycle/alias rejection and source capture. These are capture/admission paths; no steady-state allocation or timing claim is made.
findings.verification: One breadth-first replacement-model graph walk with caller arena storage replaces namespace, inventory and active capture copies. Original callback order, per-root aliases and retained-link replay preserved. Matching normal production build and seven existing core suites passed; no live capture, zero-growth or speed claim.

findings.summary: Unified/selected mark fragment ABI conversion allocates per impact while equivalent native/remote conversion uses bounded stack storage.
findings.caller: q3n event/weapon impact -> q3n_marks_impact -> marks.c impact -> events.options.mark_fragments; Unified runtime installs fragments() at runtime_services.c:499. Stock impact supplies capacity 128 (presentation/q3_native/marks.c:15-18).
findings.replacement: One mark-fragment ABI conversion helper over qa_scene_world_mark_fragments with caller/frame-arena scratch; reuse the native 128-fragment bounded behavior for stock calls instead of allocating a heap array for every impact.
findings.semantics: Keep projection/clipping, temporary and retained marks, point/fragment counts, uint32 external-word conversion, and each source world/scratch ownership. This is live impact allocation, not content admission.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof
findings.original_summary: Unified/selected Q3 impact marks allocate per effect, while native/legacy-remote adapters duplicate the same fragment conversion with stack storage.

independent_review.conclusion: Unified/selected mark fragment ABI conversion allocates per impact while equivalent native/remote conversion uses bounded stack storage.

source_evidence.evidence: fragments allocates capacity-sized rows and frees at 283.
marks allocates capacity-sized rows and frees at 142.
Uses qa_scene_mark_fragment native[128] over the same scene world fragment service.
Uses the same 128-fragment conversion pattern.

independent_review.narrowing: Common clipping already has one implementation; duplicated adapters and transient allocation remain. Stock 128 is not a license to reject a valid larger composed/mod request. A shared helper must honor actual caller capacity through common frame scratch, retaining width conversion and source world.

findings.summary: Camera/debug draw adapters use an unreserved disposable common arena per view.
findings.caller: frontend presentation/source scene -> frontend_tools_camera/frontend_tools_debug every view; debug snapshot allocates whenever retained lines exist; active camera playback samples use its supplied scratch.
findings.replacement: Use frontend->frame.storage or a load-sized caller-owned tools scratch reset at the fixed frame boundary; delete disposable arena construction/destruction in these draw adapters.
findings.semantics: Preserve camera playback timeline/portal exclusion, per-seat views and debug lifetime/instant-line expiry. No allocation claimed when camera is inactive and debug store empty.
findings.verification: Camera samples use frontend frame storage and common arena text. Current debug snapshots already use the same frame arena; no disposable per-view arena remains at the named adapters. Matching normal build and seven core suites passed; no live or performance claim.
findings.original_summary: Live camera/debug presentation creates and destroys an unreserved common arena per view, so active tools bypass load-sized frame storage.

independent_review.conclusion: Camera/debug draw adapters use an unreserved disposable common arena per view.

source_evidence.evidence: Camera path creates scratch={0}, passes it to playback and destroys it at 516.
Debug path creates scratch={0}, snapshots/draws and destroys it at 527.
Nonempty debug store snapshots lines through qa_arena_alloc.

independent_review.narrowing: The arena implementation itself is common, not duplicated. Finding is load-sized storage bypass when tools actually need scratch. Inactive camera/empty debug need not allocate; reserve from actual playback/debug workload and preserve per-view lifetime.

findings.summary: Live wheel refreshes full item definitions and label copies, growing its own three buffers on larger catalogs.
findings.caller: frontend frame wheel step (frame.c:266) -> qa_hud_wheel_update -> observe -> options.items -> wheels.c items; open/select/carousel also read the same rows.
findings.replacement: Retain item registry definitions/label IDs at admission or definition revision, reserve rows for the admitted item capacity at load, and update only count/availability from common inventory; use common frame scratch for transient rows.
findings.semantics: Keep arbitrary composed item catalog order, powerup versus weapon filtering, ammunition overrides and selection identity. Do not truncate mods or overwrite rows while the wheel borrows them.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof
findings.original_summary: The live weapon/powerup wheel rebuilds definitions and label text and can realloc its own three buffers during play.

independent_review.conclusion: Live wheel refreshes full item definitions and label copies, growing its own three buffers on larger catalogs.

source_evidence.evidence: Queries count then full definitions again at 28.
Definitions/rows realloc on larger total; labels realloc at 37.
Copies every label on each items callback before inventory/availability read.

independent_review.narrowing: After sufficient capacity there is no unconditional realloc, but enumeration and copying repeat. Common inventory definitions are the authority; derivative UI rows are legitimate borrowed presentation storage. Revision binding must preserve provider visibility, composed items, ordering and inventory changes; no arbitrary catalog cap.

findings.summary: Active menu factories rebuild heap-backed metadata on draw, not solely on opening the menu.
findings.caller: frontend presentation.c:548 -> qa_ui_draw -> ui_active -> registered factory each draw (ui/draw.c:420), also active input events. Downloads factory refreshes/copies all jobs, rotation frees/reparses all maps, browser reconstructs details/search buffers and entry arrays.
findings.replacement: Common load-owned arena/pool plus revision-gated retained IDs/rows for persistent menus; shared frame arena for truly temporary server-entry/search work. Rebuild only changed job/rotation/server metadata and filter changes.
findings.semantics: Preserve asynchronous progress display, selected stable download IDs, ordered duplicate rotation entries, browser protocol-lane merge and filter/sort semantics, and UI borrowed row lifetime. These are active menu frame allocations, not merely open-time constructors.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof
findings.original_summary: Downloads, rotation and server-browser menu factories rebuild heap-backed metadata on every draw even when identity/order is unchanged.

independent_review.conclusion: Active menu factories rebuild heap-backed metadata on draw, not solely on opening the menu.

Details factory rebuilds details.

findings.summary: Unified Q3 scans committed configstrings at frame admission and reparses reached serverinfo during current/basis reads and frame settings.
findings.caller: Unified presentation prepare -> client receive compares all QA_Q3_CONFIGSTRINGS; source_read/source_current are called through q3n_compiled frame/child validity; runtime frame_settings reparses dmflags every projected frame.
findings.replacement: Retain parsed serverinfo fields at reliable configstring admission and use existing per-index config revisions/handles. Stage only changed configstrings rather than text-compare the entire dictionary; current() compares serials/IDs without rebuilding parsed basis.
findings.semantics: Keep authoritative versus reached configstring timing and intermediate writes invisible until their command is consumed; preserve g_gametype, sv_maxclients, level-start and dmflags source semantics. Do not make the newest server dictionary prematurely visible to an older snapshot.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof
findings.original_summary: Unified Q3 recomputes names/configuration state on frame receipt and validity reads instead of retaining decoded state by config revision.

independent_review.conclusion: Unified Q3 scans committed configstrings at frame admission and reparses reached serverinfo during current/basis reads and frame settings.

source_evidence.evidence: Noninitial receive compares every configstring against committed authority and appends cs only on changes.
source_basis parses reached g_gametype/sv_maxclients/level start.
source_current calls source_read/source_basis, including prepared history fallback.
frame_settings reads configstring 0 revision but reparses dmflags every call.
Intermediate configstring event writes are intentionally not directly reached by client.

independent_review.narrowing: Authority and reached gamestate are required distinct versions. Do not collapse them or expose newest server dictionary to old snapshot. Derived parsing can be revision-gated; admission needs committed change metadata before removing comparison loop. No config loss or measured cost proved.

findings.summary: The 64-slot command history is the compiled Q3 cgame ABI command window, includes locally synthesized committed configstrings/map_restart, and is not merely a second copy of output events.
findings.caller: Remote Unified presentation ring delivery -> source_command_event -> frontend_unified_q3_client_server_command -> tokenize/copy/append into h->commands; snapshots commands() reaches frontend_unified_q3_client_command and reads the second history. receive() separately manufactures cs/map_restart commands into it.
findings.replacement: One received output-ring store with this client/snapshot consumer cursor and retained leases, plus sequence mapping only at the Q3 cgame ABI boundary. Delete the internal command-copy pool/history after readers migrate.
findings.semantics: Keep Q3 server-command sequence, ordered configstring reachability before snapshot dispatch, recipient filtering, map_restart handling and legacy ABI retention expectations; the replacement must preserve records until each internal reader retires them. Existing fixed storage avoids heap but still duplicates the event store.
findings.verification: independent source/caller refutation; exclude original claim from work list
findings.original_summary: Unified Q3 command delivery copies output events into a private 64-slot reliable history and the snapshot reader consumes that history rather than a ring cursor.

independent_review.conclusion: The 64-slot command history is the compiled Q3 cgame ABI command window, includes locally synthesized committed configstrings/map_restart, and is not merely a second copy of output events.

source_evidence.evidence: append retains one token record per command in load-sized common pool; existing records shared by history_clone at 260.
Receive creates cs commands from committed dictionary differences; 314 creates map_restart command. Those need not exist as equivalent received events.
Output commands enter history only for matching client/provider; intermediate configstring writes intentionally ignored at 1126.
Command reads enforce sequence window; newly reached cs updates reached gamestate and per-index revision at 646-655.
Sealing sets snapshot.server_command_number after admitted command delivery.
Snapshots consume commands through frozen server_command_number before scene callback.

independent_review.narrowing: Reliable ABI retention, tokenization, synthetic command sequence mapping, transactional history rollback and reached configstrings are required. Common qa_pool/qa_arena are already used and unchanged commands are reference-shared. A generic shared command-window primitive may replace duplicate implementations while preserving semantics, but a received output cursor alone cannot represent synthetic cs/map_restart or the frozen command cutoff. Do not delete the ABI history or claim this proves an event producer bypass.

findings.summary: PlayerStateToEntityState projection is independently implemented in Unified and legacy-remote Q3 snapshot caches.

findings.semantics: Preserve EF_DEAD, invisible pm types/gib threshold, trajectory types, external-event priority, two-event queue sequence mutation/event bits, powerup mask and all external field widths. Identical Q3 game semantics do not justify separate algorithms by transport.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Q3 actor-to-source-number conversion scans snapshot bindings for rendering and all published entities for trace hits.

scene_actor invokes this reverse lookup per model ownership.
Trace conversion checks up to 1022 q3n_compiled entities.
Existing common actor index supports retained full-generation identities.

Use qa_actor_index retained semantics with registry and generation rather than naively packing a whole actor into qa_string_id. Preserve first-match behavior if multiple source slots can refer to one actor. No measured slowdown proved.

findings.summary: Visible actor submission performs linked cache lookup and can construct model/brush/flare resources on a miss.
findings.caller: presentation/source -> frontend_visuals_submit per visible actor/part -> visual_owner, brush_read, model_read; cached lookups linearly walk providers/models/brushes and flare images. A miss reaches owner calloc/VFS clone/script loading or model/brush/image decoding inside that submission.

findings.semantics: Preserve VFS search policy, replacement acquisition rank, Q1 translation variants, model/source leases and cross-game resource family. Constructor misses are conditional, not an assertion that every ordinary frame allocates. Render must still support late module/mod admission at the proper load boundary.

independent_review.conclusion: Visible actor submission performs linked cache lookup and can construct model/brush/flare resources on a miss.

brush_read linked lookup; miss constructs resource/geometry/scene at 519-541.
model_cached scans model ids/resources/translation variants.
Flare image linked lookup; miss allocates/loads.
Per-part submission calls these lookup/admission helpers.

Current model/brush names are already canonical ids, so do not claim all these sites rehash names. Adopt common indexes and move late resource admission to actual load/publication boundary while preserving VFS replacement/translation/lease semantics.

findings.summary: Q1 player palette translation is copied despite an existing image translation primitive.
findings.caller: Local appearance model palette/cache and held-model network projection call their private translation loops; remote Q1 model admission runs a third loop. qa_image_player_translation already implements the same top/bottom ramps.

findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Angle/origin/scale-to-model transform construction is repeated in local visuals, view weapons, statics and remote Q1 presentation.
findings.caller: Every local visible model part, local legacy view weapon, admitted Q1 static, and every remote Q1 entity constructs identity then angle axes then copies origin/axes/scale by hand.

findings.verification: Seven local and remote model-transform callers use the common constructor with explicit angle math and uniform scale. Two helpers and four inline builders deleted. Existing model suite verifies handedness, scale-before-translation and cardinal yaw for all angle rules. Prebuilt beam placement is untouched. Source/build/core only.

findings.summary: The custom monster selection/roster UI rejects Q3 geometry and product selection clears dedicated monster overrides/provider.

Cross-game composition is not invalid solely because the geometry is Q3; do not silently alter a valid saved/custom launch.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

independent_review.conclusion: The custom monster selection/roster UI rejects Q3 geometry and product selection clears dedicated monster overrides/provider.

source_evidence.evidence: map_family comes from world.geometry, unlike rule source preset.
monster adapter reports Q3 geometry unavailable.
Product selection resets existing monster overrides and removes only startup:monster-source at 916.

Match rules use world.preset/source; 774 can install separate startup:rules provider.

Retain legitimate missing authored roster/content checks, allow empty roster and available composed providers independently of BSP family, and use actual selected rules provider for capability eligibility. No actual combined startup failure reproduced.

findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Q1 addon contact, frame-tick and rotating-target arrays are allocated lazily by live touch/use callbacks rather than during load; zero-count restores reintroduce that first-use allocation.
findings.caller: Shipped native Q1 use/touch dispatch in maps/runtime.c:1402-1421,1466-1489 reaches fog activation, addon field contact, light-ramp use and rotating-door use. Light-ramp initialization (addon_visuals.c:237-258) enables use without reserving frame_ticks; its first use adds the roster at :266. Rotating-door first use links at hipnotic_rotation.c:290. Fog touch/set_fog and push/shelter contacts call q1_map_addon_contact(...,true). These rules run in rerelease addon/MG modes and Q1 components selected in combined sessions.
findings.replacement: Prepare all three capacity-sized arrays in the existing q1_map_runtime cold bind/load path using common load-sized arena/pool storage; restore the reservation regardless of saved live-entry count, then deserialize only live rows. Delete the runtime calloc branches. No second contact or tick authority is needed.
findings.semantics: Keep actor-id/serial checks and clearing on release, cloned contact state, prepend tick-roster order, removal/reentrant callback behavior, source-time fog/deadline rules and rotation ownership/type values. Loading may allocate; the confirmed defect is that normal gameplay and a zero-entry restored state still allocate on first activation.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Q1 actor/player/map extension storage has three private grow-on-demand spare/retired pools, with calloc reachable during spawn; checkpoint publication discards unused capacity.
findings.caller: qa_q1_game_clone -> q1_create/create_state -> allocate_state and q1_map_clone -> q1_map_allocate; Hipnotic func_spawn and live gremlin split invoke clone. Native explosions.c:28 and hipnotic_weapons.c:117,294,310 create runtime timer/weapon actors. qa_q1_game_create reserves only actors/players pointer tables at runtime.c:703-704; no complete extension pool is prepared. Restore actors() allocates only serialized live actors, candidate spare lists start NULL, and restore_commit frees the previous storage and installs that candidate.
findings.replacement: Use the existing qa_pool/qa_arena implementation (include/qa/pool.h:22-38) for load-sized Q1 extension payloads instead of three local malloc/free-list implementations; retain retirement at the existing safe frame boundary. Cold restore must prepare the complete available capacity, not only occupied saved nodes.
findings.semantics: Q1 q1_actor/q1_player/q1_map_state rule tails themselves are legitimate and must remain. Preserve source-edict allocation identity, stable payload addresses, active/retired/spare lifetimes, nested observation safety, exact source continuation/save fields and no reuse before the existing prepare_frame/map_frame_begin retirement boundary. This is storage implementation duplication and play-time growth, not a request to collapse authored Q1 state into Q2/Q3 rules.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Native Q1 clone duplicates inventory snapshot acquisition with a temporary heap array despite the common pooled snapshot API.
findings.caller: Hipnotic func_spawn use (maps/runtime.c:1433 -> hipnotic_spawn.c:110), and gremlin gore/split (gremlin.c:234 -> :146) call qa_q1_game_clone during play. Clone first copies rule state/body/combat, then mallocs and frees the inventory entry array at clone.c:159-168.
findings.replacement: qa_inventory_entries_snapshot + qa_inventory_snapshot_release already perform the same two-pass entry read using the inventory service common pool-backed arena (inventory.c:924-950; inventory_internal.h:63-66, cold reservation inventory.c:478). Acquire that lease, pass entries to qa_inventory_create_actor, and release it on every success/failure path; delete the local count/overflow/malloc/free implementation.
findings.semantics: Preserve the complete entry ordering/counts/definitions, callbacks during inventory reads/creation, actor retirement checks and clone rollback/release. The canonical inventory remains authoritative; only temporary snapshot storage changes. The existing per-game gremlin clear-ammo and spawn-template rules remain distinct.
findings.verification: Q1 clone and MG3 upgrade use the common inventory snapshot lease. The shared reader retains the second enumeration for an empty inventory and MG3 between-read checkpoint; both paths release on every exit. No live or performance claim.

findings.summary: Hipnotic rotation and addon toss rediscover target-name membership by scanning all actors instead of using the common target-name index.
findings.caller: maps/runtime.c:1615 -> q1_map_rotation_think -> continuous/train/door ticks -> transform_targets -> target_snapshot. Continuous/train updates schedule every .02 seconds and door ticks every .01. link_targets and damage_targets also use the private snapshot. maps/runtime.c:1611 -> addon brush cascade uses another full snapshot, then targetname and _toss_origin filtering.
findings.replacement: Capture matching target ids through qa_targets_next/q1_snapshot_targets using the existing target index. Preserve the old host-actor-slot order by sorting the captured snapshot by actor slot before callbacks where needed; current qa_targets_next ordering is source-order and is not an unconditional drop-in. Retain empty-text guard and map/native/toss-marker predicates, and delete the full-registry target filtering implementation.
findings.semantics: The current q1_snapshot_actors returns all shared actors in host slot order, while the target index orders by authored Source order then host slot. Rotation must continue to admit foreign/QC/native bound targets in combined mode and preserve callback mutation/retirement behavior. For toss cascade retain the source bounds-center/speed nearest calculation and initial 16384 limit; changing actor iteration or using map-only candidates without proof would change behavior.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Every active addon frame captures the entire actor registry and immediately overwrites the result with its already-known frame-tick roster.
findings.caller: The Q1 Source begin_frame callback (runtime.c:544-553, installed at :896) calls q1_map_addon_frame each native tick. When light ramps/ropes/bobbing/rotating brushes have active frame entries, q1_snapshot_actors enumerates qa_actors_next for every actor before addon_visuals.c:218-219 replaces both count and ids with frame_ticks.
findings.replacement: Acquire an appropriately reserved qa_builtin_snapshot_frame directly via qa_builtin_snapshot_acquire, copy only frame_ticks, and retain the same lease across iteration; remove qa_builtin_observations from this route. The common snapshot pool must be load-prepared as part of its storage adoption, not warmed by a needless registry scan.
findings.semantics: Retain prepend roster order, immutable leased ids while callbacks add/remove actors or tick entries, visual() revalidation and release on failure. This removes an unused O(all-actors) observation, not the necessary per-tick authored update or reentrant snapshot.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Several live Q1 classifications still decode interned identifiers and compare text, and addon push scans all native actors for a known classname.
findings.caller: Bot world metadata at app/application/bot_world_bind.c:77 and Rogue native source projection at native_q1_composition_rogue.c:595 invoke qa_q1_bot_entity_read. Native trigger_push contact calls horde_manager on each non-MG3 push. Scheduled Hipnotic finale continuation and Rogue ending run decode known callback/endpoint names each invocation. Addon toss cascade decodes its load-interned marker for every candidate.
findings.replacement: Compare existing qa_string_id values for worldspawn and horde_manager (runtime_names are interned in runtime.c:718-720); use the common authored-target iteration with the same active native predicate where horde existence is needed. Intern the finite endpoint/callback/toss literal ids at cold definition load and compare ids at runtime, or use an existing typed continuation action for dispatch. Delete the text decoder/comparison copies, without adding context wrappers or a second name table.
findings.semantics: Preserve source-owned names, exact callback meaning/unknown-continuation failure and endpoint1->stage2/endpoint2->stage4 rule. horde_manager currently means any active native actor with that classname, not only one with Q1_MAP_HORDE_MANAGER kind; q1_map_horde_present adds a kind predicate and must not replace it blindly. Bot projection retains current model/classname/frame/max-health semantics and shared Source membership.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Finite binary32 narrowing is privately reimplemented in five addon modules, while Gremlin weapon aim owns a separate angle-vector/normalization implementation outside common math.
findings.caller: Fog contact/use blending, sacrifice animation, cooldown/deadline trigger/brush use and recurring authored particles run the repeated finite narrowing. Gremlin native frame actions (mission_monsters.c:119-123 -> gremlin.c:433/436 and its weapon attack path) fire nail/laser/shotgun/missile/lightning through aim(), which calls its private normalize/vectors. Addon teleport particles perform another staged-square/sqrt normalization in their scheduled particle step.
findings.replacement: Consolidate the identical finite-narrowing arithmetic beneath common numeric/math primitives, leaving feature-specific error/reporting and destination assignment at callers. Shared qa_angle_vectors/qa_vec_normalize already exist, but do not express the current full-double-radian/trig/final-narrowing and staged float-square/double-sqrt/double-reciprocal policies. Add only the source-required arithmetic policy to the single common implementation after checking its qsrc semantics; delete local math implementations rather than replace them with a non-equivalent existing variant.
findings.semantics: Five finite helpers reject nonfinite or abs(value)>=0x1.ffffffp127, saturate the narrow gap above FLT_MAX and otherwise cast; double deadline destinations retain that float-rounded result. Gremlin aim_float separately preserves NaN/infinity, uses rounded float square/add steps, double sqrt/reciprocal and full-double AngleVectors intermediates. Teleport particles retain double random-input components before the staged square rounding. Blind FLOAT/NATIVE AngleVectors or float-reciprocal normalization would change numerical output. Original gameplay spread/RNG/order stays rule data; source review establishes duplication/missing policy, not that every existing arithmetic quirk is qsrc-correct.
findings.verification: Shared finite-rounding/vector primitives and migrated callers checked against original QC, WinQuake, Hipnotic and MG1 arithmetic; normal build and seven core suites passed. Private wide TS arithmetic was corrected to qsrc rather than preserved. No live or performance claim.

findings.summary: Addon lightning contains a second complete three-ray trace/deduplicate/particle/damage loop alongside q1_electric_rays.
findings.caller: maps/runtime.c:1405 -> q1_map_addon_effect_use -> lightning() emits the beam and invokes lightning_damage() at addon_effects.c:220-221. Native weapon/expansion callers use q1_electric_rays/q1_lightning_rays for the same three parallel rays and hit deduplication. Both compute side=(-delta.y*16,-delta.y*16,0).
findings.replacement: Use one ray traversal/deduplication implementation with the actual caller policy data needed by addon effects and weapons. Existing q1_electric_rays supplies most traversal and Q1_LIGHTNING_REMEMBER_ALL/PARTICLES behavior, but requires explicit policy for source-vs-hit event actor, exact count conversion and callback continuation; delete lightning_damage after the complete caller migration. Do not introduce another ray function with the same loop.
findings.semantics: Addon remembers every hit before checking damageability, ignores failed combat reads, emits source-actor particles with count=(int32_t)(damage*4) and then applies damage, and stops when its map effect owner ceases to exist. Electric rays remember only damageable hits unless REMEMBER_ALL, propagate non-NOT_FOUND read failures, use ceilf(blood), emit hit-actor events and check inflictor liveness. Preserve those policies as data; a direct call with flags alone would currently be non-equivalent. Keep the authored side-vector expression and event/damage order until original source explicitly warrants a behavior change.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: MG3 upgrade pickup allocates a private composed-inventory snapshot during live touch instead of the common pooled inventory snapshot.
findings.caller: qa_q1_game_touch -> q1_pickup_touch -> mg3_upgrade_touch -> q1_mg3_upgrade; the original MG3 upgrade rule directly iterates the composed inventory to clamp overflowing Q1 ammo counts.
findings.replacement: qa_inventory_entries_snapshot plus qa_inventory_snapshot_release already expose the canonical pooled inventory snapshot; migrate this allocation/copy/free to that lease.
findings.semantics: Retain canonical composed entries, Q1 ammo-only filtering, count/capacity mutation and checks after callback-induced player retirement; release the lease on every exit.
findings.verification: Q1 clone and MG3 upgrade use the common inventory snapshot lease. The shared reader retains the second enumeration for an empty inventory and MG3 between-read checkpoint; both paths release on every exit. No live or performance claim.

findings.summary: Rogue rune carrier extension allocates and frees state during live frame/touch/drop instead of load-sized common-pool storage.

findings.replacement: Keep existing qa_actor_index for full actor identity, create it at game load and allocate rune rows from one load-sized qa_pool (or canonical per-player extension storage).
findings.semantics: Retain per-player rune flags/timers, full registry/generation identity, insertion order list and callback checks; free/recycle only after actor release, with no first-touch heap growth.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Q1 HUD, damage/AI/source rules and live effects still resolve or byte-compare fixed names and re-intern already-retained client names instead of runtime IDs.
findings.caller: frontend Q1 HUD/wire stats -> qa_q1_player_ui_read each displayed frame; q1_wire_board_observe -> intern(view.name) even though qa_q1_source_client_view carries name_id; combat context -> strcmp victim/killer names; monster pain/retaliation, trigger hurt/changelevel touches, MG3 upgrade/shard pickups, weapon/backpack drops, Rogue split/lava impacts, power timer/combo/empathy/vengeance and token award paths reach the fixed-name sites.

Use view.name_id directly and compare interned player name IDs. MG3 arbitrary q1:ammo/ classification needs a retained admission flag or ID membership preserving mod-defined Q1 ammo, rather than a prefix scan per upgrade.
findings.semantics: Keep original item bits, same-netname equality (not actor equality), case-sensitive classname/rune/cause spelling, localization keys and mission messages. Resolve arbitrary external text at its boundary; do not remove dynamically authored names or restrict prefix-classified mod ammo to only stock enum rows.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Rogue flag snapshot privately heap-allocates/sorts a live stable actor list instead of shared snapshot storage.
findings.caller: native_q1_composition_rogue flag capture/scoring and flag/player update call qa_q1_source_rogue_flags_snapshot, then callbacks may return/drop/remove flags.
findings.replacement: Use the common qa_builtin_snapshot_frame pool/actor snapshot lease and existing source-order comparator; keep one shared snapshot ownership API rather than malloc/free vectors.
findings.semantics: Capture all actual Rogue flags, including currently nonsolid/unlinked ones, in ascending original source_slot order; preserve full actor IDs and callback-induced retirement safety. A linked broadphase-only query would change behavior.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Q1 actor/player/map-extension storage repeats private spare/retirement pools with live calloc fallback; physical wire edicts also grow by realloc on live spawn.
findings.caller: Application control -> qa_q1_player_postthink -> q1_fire -> q1_projectile_spawn/q1_create -> create_state -> allocate_state and q1_wire_allocate_slot. Power pickups and later player/bot/component attachment reach q1_player_allocate. Shared target dispatch -> qa_q1_game_map_defer_targets -> q1_map_timer -> q1_map_allocate; delayed removal and finale timers use the same live path. qa_q1_game_create allocates pointer tables but not the extension rows; begin_world starts edicts at max_clients+1 and authored spawn grows them further, not to the complete runtime capacity.
findings.replacement: Prepare distinct typed instances of the one qa_pool at game/map load for actor, player and map-extension payloads, then use qa_pool_take/release. Reserve physical edict backing at load to its configured limit/capacity and stop growing it during play; source ordinals remain protocol metadata rather than becoming canonical actor IDs.
findings.semantics: Keep actor full registry/generation identity and native per-game extension fields. Preserve next-frame retirement: callbacks retain pointers after actor release, so returning a slot immediately can alias a replacement in the same frame. Preserve source edict 600/768 limits, original first-free/time-delay allocation and QW last-edict replacement semantics; do not collapse the protocol ordinal into actor slot.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Q1 model/sound resource-ID to original precache ordinal lookup is implemented twice as a linear scan on live wire/event paths instead of the common keyed index.
findings.caller: Native NQ/QW entity snapshot readers -> qa_q1_wire_index for every model; output sound/model records -> qa_q1_wire_emission_index. Unified Q1 presentation event conversion also uses the emission lookup.
findings.replacement: One qa_id_index-backed lookup owned by each ordered precache table, built/reserved alongside admission; both receipt and emission adapters read that index. Keep ordered rows for exact protocol serialization.
findings.semantics: Keep model/sound table distinction, empty slot zero, first precache occurrence and original expansion/QW ordinal ordering. A common implementation can have separate model and sound instances; do not reorder assets or widen legacy fields.
findings.verification: Ordered Q1 model/sound precache rows and checkpoint fields unchanged; shared ID indexes built at admission and restore replace receipt/emission scans. Source review, matching normal build and seven existing core suites passed. No live game or performance claim.

findings.summary: Q1 missing-target lookup falls back to scanning its private actor-pointer table even on the shipped path already wired to the canonical target service.
findings.caller: Monster route and addon/dragon/observer-camera target lookup -> q1_find_target. construct_q1 installs host.find_target -> qa_targets_first; when canonical lookup reports no target, q1_find_target scans every private slot. Native authored/dynamic map actors are already bound by q1_map_bind_target -> qa_targets_bind.
findings.replacement: Use the canonical qa_targets lookup as the sole implementation and return its not-found result. Standalone SDK hosts without the callback must bind the same target service rather than retaining a private scan.
findings.semantics: Preserve original first-target/source order, live name changes and missing-target behavior. Do not restrict lookup to Q1-owned targets in composed worlds. Callback absence in standalone SDK use needs an explicit common-service binding before deleting the fallback.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Rogue player-to-team-state identity lookup still capacity-scans Q1 actors repeatedly during mode field reads despite full actor identity primitives and an already-retained state reference.
findings.caller: Rogue mode q1_read/q1_write -> application_native_q1_rogue_number_read/write -> application_native_q1_rogue_state_current -> qa_q1_rogue_state_find, repeated before/after each field access. Mode member already retains p->q1.rogue_state. Initial qa_q1_rogue_state also scans before and after creation.
findings.replacement: Use the retained full state actor reference for read/current paths; index admission owner-to-state relation with common qa_actor_index or store it in the canonical player extension, enforcing uniqueness once and updating it on creation/release.
findings.semantics: Owner comparison uses source-reference semantics, while live validity still checks full registry/generation. Preserve one team-state actor per actual source client, original fields and callback retirement, and rebuild the relation on restore instead of another copied actor cache.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Q1 source userinfo keeps two private backslash-pair decoders and a grow-one-row dictionary beside the common info iterator/index primitives.
findings.caller: NQ/QW/native roster admission and Unified/bot userinfo changes -> qa_q1_source_client_userinfo[_named] -> userinfo; guest Q3 component client adapter in a Q1 source -> qa_q1_source_client_userinfo_storage. Console name/color edits reach info_set and realloc newly introduced keys.

Retain ordered rows in load-sized common arena/pool storage and use qa_id_index for key-to-row lookup; one shared builder is still missing for the repeated serialized info output (userinfo_read) and should own it rather than creating another hand-written codec.
findings.semantics: Keep normal admission versus storage-only side effects distinct, existing leading-prefix handling, last duplicate value with first insertion order, fallback name, Q1/QW color/team clamping and include_name behavior. External info text is a legitimate protocol boundary; the duplication is decoder/storage machinery, not a ban on decoding it.
findings.verification: Both reached reader/serializer owners and import/teardown checked. Normal build/seven core suites passed; replacement/input growth remains, no zero-allocation claim.

findings.summary: Q1 travel armor serialization repeats the same complete armor codec as canonical combat persistence instead of one shared game-state codec.

findings.replacement: Expose one qa_source_save_armor codec from the shared persistence/source I/O layer and migrate both callers; final domain validation remains there.

findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

Migrate the common builtin consumers, not a Q2-only substitute.
findings.semantics: Preserve candidate/source order, exclusions, nested callback pointer lifetime and actor-generation checks. Existing shared world trace stays the only trace; do not guess nesting limits or swallow overflow.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Instanced-coop pickup ownership reallocates on accepted live touches.

findings.summary: Q2 exact trigger and killbox clips omit the linked entity pose role, selecting the zero-valued NetQuake unrotated rule.
findings.caller: Rerelease exact trigger touch and exact func_killbox -> q2_entity_clip -> qa_collision_trace. Its inline target sets model/origin/angles but not pose_rules; the shared pose basis consults target.pose_rules, independently of the query policy.

findings.verification: Q2 exact trigger/killbox targets and gameplay traces use their retained role rules, including rerelease behavior; masks and deliberate classic-only dodge policy are preserved. findings.summary: Q2 push-trigger wind cooldown history reallocates during live player touches.

findings.semantics: Preserve original 1500 ms wind cooldown, actor-generation cleanup, push/sound order and reset behavior. No guessed recipient cap or suppressed release.

findings.summary: Q2 optional source continuation tails still allocate on live camera activation, lazy train-team movement and authored medic reinforcement spawn.
findings.caller: q2_q64_use -> native target_camera_dummy spawn -> calloc Q64 tail during map use. Separately rerelease MOVETEAM train groups generic team members at post-spawn without mover preparation; q2_train_next -> q2_move_start -> q2_mover_state lazily callocs for a func_wall/static team child. Also an authored rerelease reinforcement can choose a medic definition; medic_finish_spawn -> q2m_medic_finish_summons -> medic_positions_pass -> q2m_create_reinforcement -> qa_q2_monster_spawn -> monster_admit -> q2m_summon_initialize callocs the medic tail and its configured entries during play. Normal monster records already use qa_pool_take.
findings.replacement: Reserve the existing optional source entity-rule tails from the common load-sized entity extension pool, preparing train-team movers during the existing post-spawn grouping transaction; camera dummy activation takes a prepared slot. Keep one body/movement owner and original Q2 continuation algorithms. Reinforcement choice tails and their actual authored row counts must likewise be prepared from load-admitted definitions/content, with fixed common-pool slots for dynamically spawned medics.
findings.semantics: Retain original camera copy lifetime, team order, source speed/accel/decel and game-clock behavior. Optional tail storage is required source rules, but allocator growth during live activation is a primitive adoption gap.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Q2 perception trail and alert arrays grow on live player/monster ticks instead of being load-sized.
findings.caller: q2m_perception_begin -> q2_player_trail_step -> trail_for -> runtime_reserve; q2m_found_target -> q2m_perception_alert -> alert_for -> runtime_reserve; q2m_check_attack also creates rerelease alerts. Constructor creates indices only, and restore sizes arrays to saved count.

Remove live realloc and retain explicit capacity outcome.
findings.semantics: This finding concerns storage, not unifying distinct original perception rules or discarding saved alert/trail state.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Q2 hot monster hazards and retaliation unwrap already-interned classname IDs for repeated string identity comparisons.

Traits already carry common qa_string_id, but trait_classname converts it to text and these consumers strcmp literal Tesla names or the attacker classname.

Bind the missing classic protected-name literal telsa once at cold admission in the existing common strings table. Delete trait_classname after its last caller migrates; the same file already uses ID comparisons for Tesla attack strafe at 2055.
findings.semantics: Preserve zero-name behavior, exact case-sensitive source classname identity and the intentional classic protected-name literal telsa versus rerelease tesla_mine. Keep Q2 target-selection and species policies unchanged; no fingerprint, second name registry or added hot lookup.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof
