findings.summary: Q2 player restore reads uninitialized retained model identity fields before rebuilding the saved player presentation.
findings.caller: Shared Q2 continuation restore (save/game.c:131-134) and original-client import (save/original_level.c:300-302) call qa_q2_player_restore. It mallocs q2_client_state, assigns rule/player/info, then calls q2_player_source_identity_bind. The binder compares source_model and reads source_model_resource although neither has been initialized. Regular client admission zero-initializes the same state with calloc. Later spawn copies source_model_resource into visual.models[0].
findings.replacement: Use the same initialized client-state construction for admission and restore, or initialize the retained source identity fields before the existing common binder. Rebuild the model identity from saved name/skin through q2_player_source_identity_bind; do not add a new restore-specific identity resolver or validation layer.
findings.semantics: Keep the saved gameplay rule tail, actor/player identity and original save bytes unchanged. The source model resource is derived presentation state. The indeterminate reads are source-confirmed; no runtime reproduction was performed in this read-only audit.
findings.verification: source correction, normal production build and seven existing core suites; no live round trip

findings.summary: Rerelease-active Q2 trace and point-contents callers still select classic behavior from family rather than their retained role ruleset.
findings.caller: Weapon frame/fire paths call q2_project, whose trace is reached only after the classic early return and therefore is explicitly rerelease-only. qa_q2_game actor physics calls step recovery for rerelease/Rogue actors. Monster AI/reinforcement spawn queries, projectile impacts/radius damage and nuke tick/explosion queries also use these constructors. qa_collision_default_policy(QA_GAME_Q2) calls qa_collision_source_rules, which passes q2_rerelease=false and chooses QA_RULESET_Q2_CLASSIC. qa_world_trace_excluding forwards that policy unchanged to qa_collision_trace (world.c:217-223).
findings.replacement: Select the one qa_trace_behaviors entry from the already-retained role ruleset: c->rules for weapon presentation and g->options.rules for gameplay actors. Use the same common construction as player/spawn_select.c:9 and player/view.c:353; retain each caller mask, shape, pass actor and merge behavior. Do not recover an edition from a family selector.
findings.semantics: Classic callers must keep classic behavior. Rerelease callers need the existing rerelease clamp-fraction, secondary-plane, zero-all-solid and merged-contents conventions defined at contents.c:20 rather than classic conventions at :19, including combined sessions on foreign BSP content. The classic-only dodge trace at projectiles.c:120 is deliberately excluded. No live impact measurements were made.
findings.verification: Q2 exact trigger/killbox targets and gameplay traces use their retained role rules, including rerelease behavior; masks and deliberate classic-only dodge policy are preserved. Source correction, matching frozen-tree normal production build and seven existing core suites; no live game, audio, install, timing or whole-frame allocation proof.

findings.summary: Medic reinforcement payloads bypass pooled monster storage and allocate/free during live resurrection or authored reinforcement spawning.
findings.caller: medic.c:441 invokes q2m_revive, which calls monster_admit with previous state (core.c:1971-1983). Only rerelease transfers previous->summons, so a revived classic Rogue medic/commander reaches summon_initialize with no payload and calloc executes. Authored reinforcement choices can also spawn a medic through q2m_create_reinforcement -> qa_q2_monster_spawn -> monster_admit. configure allocates its entries on first configure, and q2m_free_monster frees the companion payload while the main monster itself uses the common qa_pool (core.c:1997-2013).
findings.replacement: Reserve optional summon state and authored reinforcement-entry storage at load/admission with the shared qa_pool/qa_arena primitives alongside the existing monster pool (game.c:397-400). Take/release companion records with the same ownership and source-frame retirement lifetime; resolve authored choices before runtime use where their extent is known.
findings.semantics: Preserve classic versus rerelease transfer behavior, reinforcement definitions/order, strength and slot accounting, RNG draws, move callbacks and delayed lease retirement. This finding is about concrete revive/authored-spawn paths, not a claim that every stock base1 frame allocates.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Using the Q2 rerelease compass grows private path storage on the live item-action path.
findings.caller: Player item commands (player/commands.c:181-190) or the shared inventory item action reach qa_q2_item_use -> q2_item_use_duration -> item_use_duration. COMPASS dispatches to q2_client_item_action (items/powers.c:206-207); after a valid POI is found it reallocs help_points to 129 positions on first use, or when restored storage is smaller. Normal client admission starts the rule tail at zero.
findings.replacement: Reserve the fixed 129-point extent once when the player/map state is admitted, using shared load-sized pool/arena storage. The live compass action should fill existing storage and update its indices rather than reallocating it.
findings.semantics: Keep the 128 navigation points plus the possible inserted nearby look point, selected POI, reached/unreached result and marker/audio order. Allocation occurs on live user activation, not every render frame.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Q2 FOV preferences retain a second private backslash info-string parser beside the common text primitive.
findings.caller: preferences.c:139/147 parse and rewrite the source userinfo during qa_q2_player_field_of_view_set. Application native FOV changes (view_preferences.c:110) and initial character userinfo projection (character_selection.c:213) use the same writer. The admission path already uses common qa_info_find, while preferences implements its own info_pair and pair_read parser.
findings.replacement: Use qa_info_find with first-match policy for FOV reads and qa_info_next borrowed pairs for the writer. Retain FOV-specific bounds and number conversion as caller policy; remove the private pair reader/type rather than adding another parser.
findings.semantics: Preserve optional initial backslash, malformed-tail termination, first duplicate FOV value, first-key ordering/deduplication in the rewritten info string, and current saturating decimal-prefix integer conversion. The writer is reached on preference changes/admission, so this is a duplicate primitive finding rather than a claimed steady-state frame allocation.
findings.verification: Source callers migrated and replaced paths deleted; matching normal production build and seven core suites passed. No live or performance claim.

findings.summary: Q2 landmark travel implements the same ordered Euler vector rotation twice instead of one shared math operation.
findings.caller: target_changelevel captures relative landmark origin and velocity with targets.c unrotate, then q2_player_spawn_select reconstructs them through rotate_landmark on the destination map. Both functions repeat the same three cosf/sinf stages; unrotate changes the input angle signs.
findings.replacement: Provide one shared ordered Euler/axis vector operation in the math primitive with explicit caller numeric/order policy, and invoke it with positive or negated angles from the two game-rule callers. Existing qa_angle_axis/qa_vec_rotate_around must not be substituted blindly if their multiplication order differs.
findings.semantics: Preserve the reached x/pitch, y/roll, z/yaw sequential float operations, negation before radians conversion, qsrc landmark position/velocity behavior and the caller-specific view-angle travel rule. Do not turn this adoption into a correction of inverse-matrix conventions.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Q2 nuke reaction and spawn-point admission convert retained classname identities back to text for fixed-name comparisons.
findings.caller: qa_q2_damage_reaction -> qa_q2_projectile_reaction (mines.c:943-944) -> q2_nuke_reaction resolves the attacker definition to text and strcmp compares nuke although the launch producer stores runtime_names[Q2_NAME_RESOURCE_NUKE]. Authored entity spawn (entities/lifecycle.c:127) calls q2_player_map_spawn, which string-compares five info_player classnames even though the same runtime IDs are already retained and used by spawn_select/intermission.
findings.replacement: Compare the existing qa_string_id fields directly against the once-bound runtime_names entries. Keep the classification and damage-reaction branches in the Q2 rule layer; delete only the text resolution/strcmp copies.
findings.semantics: Preserve adjacent-nuke release versus detonation, rerelease-only lava spawns and existing coop/deathmatch eligibility. Spawn-point classification here is admission-time; the nuke comparison is a live damage callback.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: The Q2 rerelease game RNG and frontend footstep RNG duplicate the MT19937 seed/twist/temper primitive.
findings.caller: Gameplay AI/weapon/spawn rules call q2_rerelease_word through q2_random helpers. Frontend entity_footstep calls step_uniform at map_events.c:824, whose private step_random repeats the same 624-word initialization, twist and temper kernel. The frontend and gameplay streams have intentionally separate state and sampling policies.
findings.replacement: One common MT19937 primitive with separate instance state for gameplay and presentation. Keep the bounded sampling wrappers as policy where they intentionally use different rejection algorithms; expose the shared state in the existing checkpoint/save boundaries without changing its wire representation.
findings.semantics: Preserve seeds, twist order, tempering, every gameplay draw count, frontend independent stream, multiply-high gameplay rejection versus frontend modulo rejection, and source save state. This duplicates J14-11 context and should be deduplicated in the combined audit rather than counted as a second issue.
findings.verification: Source callers migrated and replaced paths deleted; matching normal production build and seven core suites passed. No live or performance claim.

findings.summary: Q3 bounds/radius observations use a lazy heap-grown builtin snapshot pool during gameplay instead of the load-sized shared world snapshot storage.
findings.caller: Q3 missile splash -> q3_radius -> q3_bounds_snapshot; kamikaze think -> kamikaze_area -> q3_bounds_snapshot; player/holdable killbox -> q3_bounds_snapshot. qa_q3_create does not initialize snapshot_frames, so first use allocates and deeper callback nesting allocates additional frames.
findings.replacement: Migrate to qa_world_snapshot_capture/qa_world_snapshot_sort and the one load-sized world snapshot pool in src/world/spatial.c, with the existing collision-role and original source-order comparator. Delete the Q3 snapshot_frames owner and remaining lazy builtin snapshot implementation after all its callers migrate.
findings.semantics: Retain callback-safe captured actor identities, exact role filtering and source order, recheck actor liveness after callbacks, and preserve nested leases. Do not replace it with a private Q3 fixed-cap array or cap combined actor counts. The already-migrated invulnerability_overlap world snapshot is not a finding.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Q3 maintains and clears its own once-per-source-frame actor visit array instead of using qa_stamp_set.
findings.caller: The registered Q3 component actor callback and application arsenal dispatch both reach qa_q3_source_run_actor. The private bool array prevents a source actor from running twice when those paths overlap, and is memset at both frame-begin entry points.
findings.replacement: One caller-owned, load-sized qa_stamp_set (include/qa/stamp.h); begin at the Q3 source-frame boundary and mark in qa_q3_source_run_actor. Delete source_actor_ran and its private clear/test/write sites.
findings.semantics: Preserve one execution per original Q3 source frame, not per rendered/common frame, and preserve the reset of a newly rebound source slot within that frame. Actor slot reuse and nested source frames must not inherit a prior mark.
findings.verification: Q3 once-per-source-frame actor visits use the caller-owned common stamp set; new source frame, rebound slot and failure-retained mark behavior are preserved. Source correction, matching frozen-tree normal production build and seven existing core suites; no live game, audio, install, timing or whole-frame allocation proof.

findings.summary: Q3 client info-string lookup reimplements the common backslash-pair walker and ASCII case-fold match.
findings.caller: Native Q3 client join/userinfo -> qa_q3_client_slot_userinfo; selected/combined client presentation -> qa_q3_client_selected_presentation. The same exported qa_q3_client_info_value is also reached by native_q3_clients.c, client_events.c, native Q3 cgame client_info.c and bot admission.
findings.replacement: Use qa_info_find from src/core/text.c with QA_INFO_CASE_FOLD, retaining the caller boundary copy/truncation and output copy. Delete upper/key_equal/the private pair walker.
findings.semantics: Preserve first case-insensitive match, malformed-pair termination, 1023-byte source truncation and capacity-1 output truncation. qa_q3_info_value is stricter and is not an automatic drop-in for this original client ABI behavior.
findings.verification: Source callers migrated and replaced paths deleted; matching normal production build and seven core suites passed. No live or performance claim.

findings.summary: Q3 map/command and client-userinfo numeric readers privately duplicate prefix parsing already partly represented in the common numeric primitive.
findings.caller: Map field admission -> q3_map_number/q3_map_integer/q3_map_vector; setviewpos -> q3_source_atof; userinfo handicap/predict/overlay/teamtask -> source_integer. These are shipped native and combined-mode paths, not dead parser helpers.
findings.replacement: Extend the single src/core/number.c reader with explicit original Q3 VM scan and wrapping-int policies, then migrate these callers and delete the private readers. qa_parse_quake_number(QA_QUAKE_NUMBER_Q3_VM) already supplies a Q3 prefix policy; qa_q3_parse_integer is saturating and cannot replace the wrapping parser unchanged.
findings.semantics: Keep signed-byte whitespace, plus/minus, 32-bit wrap, parser cursor/overrun behavior and original arithmetic. The map reader currently uses float fractional terms while the common Q3_VM reader uses double fractional terms, so an unqualified substitution would change results. Move the exact reached rule into the common primitive rather than silently changing conversion.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Q3 retains small private angle/bounds math implementations beside existing or directly duplicated common helpers.
findings.caller: Cutscene and forced-view movement delta words -> q3_angle_word; Q3 door-team trigger construction -> inline bounds union; Team Arena kamikaze damage -> bounds_distance. Common radius damage separately uses the identical distance_to_bounds expression.
findings.replacement: Use qa_angle_to_word with QA_ANGLE_WORD_NATIVE and qa_bounds_union. Expose one bounds-distance helper in common math/world and use it from both kamikaze and builtin radius damage; delete the copied implementations.
findings.semantics: Keep the native multiply-then-divide float angle rounding and low-16-bit conversion, fminf/fmaxf behavior, nearest-box-point distance and the original per-weapon damage falloff. Door setup is a cold path, not a claimed frame-allocation issue.
findings.verification: Source callers migrated and replaced paths deleted; matching normal production build and seven core suites passed. No live or performance claim.

findings.summary: Q3 per-player end-frame loop sounds and fixed sound emitters still resolve path text and scan configstrings instead of using retained resource IDs/source indexes.
findings.caller: Application native Q3 END phase -> client_end_frame -> qa_q3_client_end_prepare -> player_end_frame. Every proxmine-ticking player calls qa_q3_sound_index, whose path interning is followed by a linear source configstring search; every active fry/tick loop is also interned again. q3_sound/q3_sound_report are reached by water damage, mover transitions, push/hurt triggers and item respawns.
findings.replacement: Bind fixed Q3 resource IDs and the corresponding original sound configstring indexes at load/map admission or configstring revision; pass IDs to the existing shared builtin sound/event path. PROXMINE_TICK is already in the load-bound runtime_names table. Keep a dynamic-ID admission path only for genuinely runtime module resources.
findings.semantics: Preserve G_FindConfigstringIndex first-free numbering/truncated name comparison, sexed sound handling, original wire event 45 and channels, and Q3 source clock. Repeated interning of existing text need not allocate, but it still performs the unnecessary name lookup; no measured speedup is asserted.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Q3 proximity mines and mixed-player accuracy conflate native numeric teams with the common session-interned qa_team_id, creating combined-mode and save/protocol correctness risks.
findings.caller: Q3 prox fire stores hooks.source_team (sess.team numeric 1/2) for native clients but combat.team (interned ID) for foreign clients. The armed-trigger check repeats those two domains and compares them directly. source_wire exports that stored value as generic1 and save.c serializes it through qa_source_save_string. Hitscan/splash accuracy uses q3_accuracy; its mixed branch compares q3-team:%i to the foreign team text, although the real adapters map to mode rule IDs and names such as team:red/team:blue or q3:1/q3:2.
findings.replacement: Keep canonical qa_team_id in shared projectile/combat state and compare it directly for all native/foreign participants. Use one load-bound original-number <-> common-team mapping at module and protocol boundaries; only wire generic1/native session state uses original Q3 1/2 values. Save the canonical identity, not an original numeric value masquerading as a string ID.
findings.semantics: Preserve original team-mode friendly-fire and mine exclusion rules, unteamed/spectator semantics and exact Q3 generic1 wire value. The source proves a domain mix; no live reproduction or particular numeric string-table collision is claimed. A native value of 1/2 can currently serialize an unrelated interned string and restore as a different ID.
findings.verification: Named source callers migrated and replaced implementation deleted; matching normal production build and seven core suites passed. No live, performance or whole-frame allocation claim.

findings.summary: Q3 spawnpoint enumeration converts retained class IDs back to text and reclassifies them, then application admission converts the enum back to the same class names.
findings.caller: Native Q3 map spawnpoint handling and application q3_player_points during travel/player admission -> qa_q3_map_spawnpoint_next. The latter runs a seven-name strcmp chain over map actor class strings; q3_player_points uses a second matching static name list and interns the selected name into qa_mode_spawnpoint.
findings.replacement: Classify spawn kind once at authored-entity admission and retain the original classname ID alongside the typed kind; return both to the common mode spawnpoint consumer. Delete the repeated name chain and enum-to-name round trip.
findings.semantics: Keep exact original case-sensitive class matching, authored ordinal, no-bot/no-human flags and Q3 spawnpoint kinds. This is a load/respawn/admission-path duplication, not a per-render-frame cost claim.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: BG_PlayerStateToEntityState projection is implemented separately in Q3 gameplay wire output, cgame predicted presentation and network prediction collision state.
findings.caller: Native Q3 CONTROL/END phases -> qa_q3_wire_player_publish -> convert_player; remote/unified native cgame frame -> q3n_packet_remote_predict -> predict; prediction-scene initial/next/transition -> player_kinematics. Full gameplay/presentation copies both implement spectator/gib type selection, trajectories, dead flags, predictable event consumption and powerup mask; collision prediction repeats the kinematic subset.
findings.replacement: One Q3 original-rule projection helper over common qa_q3_player/qa_q3_entity, with explicit snap/extrapolation and predictable-event consume/no-consume policy. Native source-field and collision-subset adapters only copy the resulting required fields.
findings.semantics: This is one original Q3 rule implementation, not a demand to erase other games rules. Preserve external-event precedence, two-slot sequence clamping/bits, mutation only in the authoritative/event-owning caller, interpolation/extrapolation clocks and snap behavior. Collision prediction intentionally must not consume source predictable events.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Q3 ranked gameplay reports bypass the shared output ring into a private heap-allocated pending-report queue.
findings.caller: Ranked native Q3 fire/hit/reward/time rule paths -> hooks.ranking_report -> application_rankings_report. The application allocates a linked row for each report and copies string text, then source-frame frame_players flushes that private queue to the ranking backend. This is distinct from the already-ring-backed ranking UI output.
findings.replacement: Typed ranking report records in the one application output ring, with a ranking consumer cursor and leased string payload, delivered by the backend phase. Delete the application_rankings reports/report_tail private queue; any unavoidable external backend transport storage remains a boundary implementation rather than a second engine event queue.
findings.semantics: Retain enabled/warmup gating, report order, accumulate flags, self/other attribution, provider identity and pending-unsent save ownership. Do not discard ranking capability or remove boundary backpressure merely to avoid allocations.
findings.verification: Current caller review confirms typed leased ranking reports, one ring cursor, synchronous provider delivery and save/restore cursor rebinding; no private pending report list. Matching recorded normal build/core checks; no external provider run.

findings.summary: Q3 target-location and native team-combat visibility privately compose point-leaf/PVS/area checks instead of one shared point-visibility query, and their area policies already differ.
findings.caller: Native Q3 team status/location chat -> qa_q3_map_team_location_read; native team defense/combat bonuses -> in_pvs. Both manually resolve two leaves, project cluster/area indexes and test visibility/connectivity. Team combat honors the retained no-areas cvar; target-location enumeration always enforces area connectivity.
findings.replacement: Add/use one common world point-to-point visibility query with caller trace scratch and explicit PVS/PHS and area policy, then route these callers through it. Keep Q3 location chain traversal and nearest-location selection as original gameplay rules.
findings.semantics: Preserve collision-vs-Q1 leaf policy, original cluster and area boundary behavior, no-areas semantics, target-location distance/tie order and callback liveness. The existing qa_world_leaf_visibility handles entity bounds and is not itself a drop-in for point-pair visibility.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Native module hardware invocation and import continuations bypass common retained storage with per-call packet/XSAVE allocations and per-entry signal-stack mmap/munmap.
findings.caller: Shipped application guest_native_q2.c:143 -> qa_native_host_run_frame (host.c:603-626 RunFrame/vmMain; ClientThink also calls qa_native_call) -> instance.c:222 native_call_binding -> process.c:210 native_process_invoke -> sysv_process.c:499/windows_process.c:373 guest_abi_invoke_native -> abi.c:795 invoke -> native_backend.c:224 guest_host_child_run_receipt -> host_child.c:726 child_run. HOST_RUN and each HOST_STOP/RESUME import allocate packet and state storage; host_x86_64_enter copies aligned state, allocates controller XSAVE and maps an alternate signal stack on every entered bridge. guest_native_transfer allocates/free aligned state on ABI CPU reads and writes.
findings.replacement: Use common qa_pool/qa_arena nesting-scoped leases for transfer buffers and load-retained aligned CPU/signal-stack storage per active continuation, extending the one owned process backend rather than adding another executor. The guest already owns scratch_pages and ABI plans/arguments use it.
findings.semantics: Preserve x86 ABI widths, 64-byte XSAVE alignment, all enabled state components, re-entrant module imports, stopped-continuation lifetimes, descriptor transfer and ordered replies. Cold constructor/checkpoint allocations are not the finding.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Native Q3 save continuation still embeds complete installed PE/ELF artifact bytes through the process provenance checkpoint.
findings.caller: Application save provider capture -> application_guest_checkpoint_capture -> native Q3 roles in guest_q3_save.c -> qa_native_process_checkpoint -> native_process_checkpoint_host -> qa_native_sysv/windows_process_checkpoint -> guest_profile_artifacts_checkpoint, which writes each original artifact.size and artifact.data.
findings.replacement: Installed module references by content/name and retained ABI metadata; mutable memory delta uses the existing qa_native_guest_baseline/source_save delta path against the externally resolved pristine artifact. Delete serialized redundant artifact bytes from ordinary game saves.
findings.semantics: Keep native/QVM/mod continuation and original mutable process state; resolve every installed dependency in order on load. The Q2 original WriteGame/WriteLevel route and module_save.c already avoid this asset embedding; do not replace them with full process snapshots.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Native import dispatch and guest file/TLS identity lookups use private linear scans instead of the common numeric-ID index; import dispatch re-scans its function registry several times per call.
findings.caller: Native Q2/Q3 RunFrame/ClientThink/vmMain -> owned process -> guest_host_child continuation -> native_backend import scans guest callbacks -> runtime_import dispatch scans descriptor IDs before/after nested service invocation. Runtime libc/UCRT/kernel fread/fwrite/getc/putc/ReadFile/WriteFile -> respective FILE/handle lookup -> guest_runtime_resources_read/write -> begin -> file_at. ELF __tls_get_addr resolves the module ID through guest_sysv_tls_address on each invocation.
findings.replacement: Use qa_id_index (include/qa/id_index.h) keyed by numeric ID/address through its uint64 discriminator, retaining the admission-order tables as the sole row storage. Resolve sparse TLS module IDs once at attachment into that index. Re-find by index after nested callbacks that may grow tables. The native_host string registry already uses this shared primitive.
findings.semantics: Preserve 64-bit foreign IDs/addresses, duplicate import aliases sharing one service, lazy binding during nested imports, existing admission order and checkpoint layout, FILE/handle close ownership, and authoritative guest DTV contents. Name-based external symbol resolution and cold restore validation are distinct and are not the hot lookup finding.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Windows UCRT printf reimplements the guest formatter and exact binary-to-decimal conversion even though the shared guest formatter already supports Windows target widths and dialects.
findings.caller: Shipped PE module -> owned Windows process -> bound __stdio_common_vsprintf descriptor (windows_crt.c:52) -> runtime_import dispatch -> windows_runtime service_invoke -> windows_crt_invoke C_PRINTF -> printf_service -> private printf_parse/float_body. The same owned module SDK variadic imports already call guest_format_render_entry in process.c:250, which selects Windows argument widths and floating dialect; SysV libc formatting uses that common implementation. Native Q3 game printing formats strings before trap_Print; qsrc game/g_main.c:246/257/547/558 provides the original formatting call paths.
findings.replacement: Keep one guest format parser/converter and extend its dialect policy for the UCRT option-dependent output sink, va_list source, rounding and error behavior; route Windows CRT through it and remove the duplicate parser/decimal/padding implementation. guest_scan_prepare/execute already follows this pattern for Windows scanf.
findings.semantics: Preserve UCRT legacy ties-away rounding (mode 4), option 32 MXCSR rounding, option 16 three-digit exponents, option 1 legacy termination and option 2 counting/truncation, Windows long/I32/I64 widths, pointer text, wide-character conversion errors, NaN spellings and %n rejection. The existing shared float routine currently admits modes 0-3 only, so a blind forwarding replacement would regress valid Windows behavior.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: SysV and Windows guest qsort each implement the same heap-sort/comparator/swap algorithm independently.
findings.caller: Native modules import qsort: guest_sysv_libc_add registers libc qsort (sysv_libc.c:98) and Windows CRT descriptor table registers qsort (windows_crt.c:42). Owned process import dispatch reaches LC_SORT or C_QSORT. The original native Q3 CalculateRanks uses qsort in qsrc quake-iii-arena/code/game/g_main.c:806; Q2 rerelease player listing uses it at rerelease/g_cmds.cpp:1151.
findings.replacement: One guest-array sorting operation using qa_native_guest_read/write, common scratch leases and a comparator invocation adapter; external ABI decoding and empty-range argument rules remain at each import boundary. No shared guest sort operation presently exists in the inspected code.
findings.semantics: Preserve comparator signed-I32 result, guest address/element widths, current callback order and equal-key behavior, partial mutations on callback failure, nested foreign comparator calls and two-element scratch lifetime. Host qsort cannot directly dereference foreign guest addresses.
findings.verification: One guest heap-sort body serves SysV and Windows imports through comparator and memory-access adapters. ABI decoding, empty-range rules, signed comparator results, callback order, ties, nested scratch and partial failure mutations remain at their existing boundaries. Normal production build and seven core suites passed; no live guest-module claim.

findings.summary: Several guest file/stream/text service implementations still allocate transient host buffers per invocation instead of using the common scoped guest scratch storage already used by adjacent services.
findings.caller: Owned native module import -> runtime_import dispatch -> sysv stdio fflush/fwrite or Windows kernel ReadFile/WriteFile/MultiByteToWideChar/GetModuleFileName/HeapReAlloc, or MSVC stream numeric insertion/transfer. The original Q2 WriteGame/WriteLevel uses fwrite repeatedly (qsrc quake-2/game/g_save.c:314/418/475/478/542/574/641/645/656/660), so these are live module services beyond cold construction. Their temporary malloc/calloc buffers are freed before returning to the caller.
findings.replacement: Use the existing guest scratch_pages qa_pool and scoped qa_arena leases for temporary snapshots/conversion output, or an existing semantics-preserving fixed transfer chunk where suitable (windows_stdio.c:247 already uses a stack chunk for binary transfers). Migrate callers and delete private heap staging; keep genuine guest allocations and opened capability ownership.
findings.semantics: Preserve full admitted lengths, fwrite snapshot stability across callbacks, nested service lifetimes, actual partial read/write receipts, rollback of file offset on a failed guest destination, Windows CRLF/Ctrl-Z behavior and foreign allocation semantics. Do not truncate to smaller arbitrary buffers or replace guest-requested malloc with an invalid new limit.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Native Q2 WriteEntity grows a private heap reference buffer during live message construction.
findings.caller: Original game module gi.WriteEntity -> native_host_import -> native_host_q2_import -> native_host_message_write; multicast/unicast then forwards payload plus actor references. Restore also resets reference capacity to saved used count.
findings.replacement: Reserve reference storage at host/map admission from maximum_message_bytes/2 (each reference consumes two wire bytes), using the common load-owned arena/pool; restore into that retained extent.
findings.semantics: Keep byte offsets, full actor generations, original int16 entity encoding, message ordering and configured message-size bound.
findings.verification: Native host message references reserve once from actual wire capacity. WriteEntity and restore reuse the span; ABI, saved fields and callback order preserved. Matching normal build and seven core suites; no live guest or performance claim.

findings.summary: Rerelease native HUD mallocs and frees the public player-state prefix on every draw.
findings.caller: application_native_q2_draw_hud -> qa_native_host_q2_player_state -> malloc(bytes), then qa_native_host_q2_draw_hud, qa_buffer_free.
findings.replacement: Read into caller-owned fixed ABI buffer (184 classic/296 rerelease bytes) or existing frame arena; expose borrowed/span output instead of owned qa_buffer.
findings.semantics: Pass the exact unmodified rerelease 296-byte SDK prefix to cgame DrawHUD; retain synchronous callback lifetime and seat isolation.
findings.verification: Native HUD player-state prefix is read directly into caller-owned ABI storage; owned heap buffer and free removed. Exact 184/296-byte data and synchronous per-seat lifetime retained. Normal build/seven core suites passed; no live claim.

findings.summary: Owned native process current checks perform bootstrap filesystem identity reads on runtime calls.

findings.verification: Removed per-call bootstrap path witness checks and unused held bootstrap descriptor. Cold native-runtime launch validation and actual owned child probe/capture remain. Other standard file capability checks remain; no live SDK claim.
