findings.summary: QVM gameplay write-watch registration can allocate private rows/ranges after load despite delivery using common pooled leases.
findings.caller: Guest Q3 item-touch/damage/composition callback scopes register qa_qvm_observe_writes(_owned) around source execution; a new range count or nested active delivery cannot reuse an inactive row and reaches calloc/malloc.
findings.replacement: Load-reserve watch records and maximum range scratch in common qa_pool/qa_arena, with binding-id lookup via common index; retire rows only after all active deliveries return.
findings.semantics: Keep exact overlapping-range merge, ordered publication/after/dispose, observer reentry and unobserve behavior, unique binding generations, and before/after RAM bytes. VM store observers are necessary synchronous write-through; do not force them into asynchronous presentation events.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: QVM damage reaction observers allocate a new private function binding for each damage scope and lazily grow the function-entry index during play.
findings.caller: application_q3_damage_scope execution calls reaction_refresh for pain/die functions before qa_qvm_proceed and again when those function pointers change during observed writes. reaction_refresh calls qa_qvm_observe_function, which always callocs new_binding, and ensure_entry reallocs/callocs a first-seen target; frame_close unbinds the observers and outer invocation collect_bindings frees them.
findings.replacement: Load-reserve the immutable image function-entry index and use the common qa_pool for active binding rows, indexed by the existing binding ID with the shared ID index. Recycle inactive rows only after every enclosing guest/observer delivery returns.
findings.semantics: Preserve the guest pain/die callbacks, callback registration order, registration-during-delivery cut at last_binding, monotonically unique binding IDs, cancellation, nested damage lifetimes and removal after active execution returns. These are synchronous source observers, not output-ring presentation events.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: QVM region hooks and evaluators rebuild immutable control-flow qualification with private heap proof states on each gameplay invocation.
findings.caller: Original Q3 combined locomotion hooks in arsenal_guest, equipment status/ammo hooks, weapon give/drop/damage hooks and delay/pickup evaluators call qa_qvm_bind_regions or qa_qvm_evaluate_(call_)region during source execution. Those APIs call qualify for the same immutable image and region each time; qualify callocs the path table/initial path and proof_edge mallocs every reachable proof state (plus locals for evaluation).
findings.replacement: Produce a qualified region descriptor once when the immutable image/profile is admitted and retain it by the existing image/region identity, not a fingerprint. Runtime bind/evaluate consumes that descriptor and keeps only its mutable invocation state in the already-adopted common frame lease. For genuinely dynamic descriptors, run admission proof in caller-owned common load-sized scratch rather than a private allocator.
findings.semantics: Preserve owner/entry/join and guest semantics identity, all forward-edge and local live-in/result checks at descriptor admission, overlap checks for multiple bound regions, exact counter/stack behavior, and reentrant per-invocation state. Do not remove the necessary bytecode admission analysis or change interpreted versus compiled execution semantics.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Browser ordering, packet decode scratch and retained datagram replacement still use private temporary heap paths instead of the shared arena/pool.
findings.caller: Startup browser refresh (startup_server_browser.c:408,425) -> frontend_network_menu_rows (network.c:7792) -> qa_server_browser_list mallocs a full ordering array, despite the caller already owning frame scratch. Incoming physical packets -> frontend network browser delivery (network.c:1391,1457) -> qa_server_browser_receive -> qa_browser_q3_receive/qa_browser_status_decode allocate decoder/result scratch; q3_store_response/status_store_response malloc and free the retained bytes on each refresh. Retail discovery -> network_kex.c:87 -> receive_kex_discovery -> same retained-response allocation. Q2 status decoder additionally mallocs each transient player name before its synchronous browser callback (connectionless.c:68).
findings.replacement: Pass the existing frame/caller qa_arena to temporary list/decode work; use the common qa_pool-backed arena with browser entry lifetimes for retained response bytes, reserving from actual admitted browser capacity and dialect packet extents. No independent private allocator or smaller arbitrary limits.
findings.semantics: Keep exact protocol decoders, address+protocol key, Q3 challenge matching, insertion/source order and sorting/filter count semantics. Retained response views must remain valid for their documented owner interval; nested changed callbacks must not reuse leased decode/result scratch. Response refresh is persistent input admission, but unconditional temporary and replacement mallocs are avoidable with existing common ownership.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: QW server output has a second Number-valued encoder and baseline/frame history beside the standard QW codec.
findings.caller: frontend/network_qw.c:184,468,1002,1022 encodes stats/baselines/players/nails through qa_qw_source_write_*; runtime/q1_qw.c:237,254 sends/stores source entities via qa_qw_source_history. Client and signon service paths instead use qa_qw_service_write and qa_qw_decoder frame/baseline storage.
findings.replacement: One QW field/delta writer and one history implementation, with module-boundary numeric conversion and an explicit source narrowing policy rather than duplicated structs/walks. Keep each peer instance and protocol dialect data.
findings.semantics: The source path deliberately wraps integer/byte/coordinate widths after integer conversion, while standard writer validates representability; preserve original module-to-wire narrowing without forcing doubles through float or silently changing range behavior. Preserve QW28/29 extensions, sorted merge, frame age and U_SOLID clear behavior. Confirmed divergence: qw_source.c delta_entity suppresses a solid true-to-false update when no other field changes (its early return lacks the force toggle); quakeworld.c write_entity explicitly forces that clear. The shared writer must keep the latter clearing behavior.
findings.verification: Writer portion source-reviewed and checked in bcb95cff, including actual SOLID transitions and QW29 extension decoding. Source/decoder history consolidation remains open.

findings.summary: Q2 connectionless replies and KEX discovery handling still allocate private temporary packet/name/address buffers while receiving live packets.
findings.caller: Incoming queue-delivered packets -> frontend network.c:1377/1454 -> frontend_network_q2_host_receive (network_q2_host.c:431) -> qa_network_q2_bootstrap_receive -> server_receive/send_text/refusal; host tick -> server_continue/acceptance. KEX transport game_dispatch (kex_transport.c:120) -> qa_kex_lan_dispatch -> message(kind129) allocates a 65535-byte reply. The same physical dispatch routes to qa_kex_mdns_owner_dispatch (kex_discovery_owner.c:226), which calls qa_kex_mdns_read/dns_name and announce on discovery questions; browser queue delivery reaches it through network.c:6343/frontend_kex_browser_dispatch.
findings.replacement: Use the existing qa_arena for synchronous response/name/address scratch, backed by owner-reserved qa_pool pages where nested callbacks need separate leases. qa_network_send_address forwards bytes synchronously to qa_net_transport_send (runtime/session.c:82), so reply builders do not require standalone malloc. Retained mDNS endpoint/address names must keep their owner lease through retain_records instead of borrowing a reset query arena. Preserve actual protocol bounds and interface enumeration; cold socket/interface admission is not the reported issue.
findings.semantics: Preserve exact OOB print/client_connect framing and URL advertisement, KEX kind129 payload and 65535-byte wire limit, mDNS compressed-name validation and Unicode folding, current interface visibility, nested transport callback lifetimes and retained endpoint replacement. This is a storage adoption gap, not a claim that wire decoders should lose their protocol-specific layouts.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: KEX userinfo projection duplicates the shared info-string iterator and allocates 256 full key/value copies for every projection.
findings.caller: Q2 bootstrap client tick -> qa_q2_handshake_poll -> qa_q2_connect_write (handshake.c:173/449) -> qa_q2_kex_client_userinfo. Server admission -> qa_network_q2_server_userinfo -> q2_server_userinfo (session_control.c:8), and a live Q2 userinfo command (session_server.c:219) use qa_q2_kex_seat_userinfo per local seat.
findings.replacement: Read borrowed key/value spans using the existing qa_info_next in src/core/text.c:8, retaining the KEX suffix-selection policy at the protocol boundary. Keep only bounded span/selection scratch in a caller-owned qa_arena or existing fixed protocol token storage; delete info_pairs and the calloc/free pair arrays. qa_info_next does not apply KEX validation, so retain the existing malformed/empty-key and 256-pair validation at this boundary.
findings.semantics: Preserve unsuffixed defaults, seat-specific _N overrides, last-selected duplicate handling, output admission order, seat capacity 8, key/value wire extents and _0 expansion on client connect. Borrowed spans must survive only the synchronous projection; output remains caller-owned.
findings.verification: Named source callers migrated and replaced implementation deleted; matching normal production build and seven core suites passed. No live, performance or whole-frame allocation claim.

findings.summary: Live Q2 split-seat unicast deduplication grows a private realloc array and linearly scans it for each message or sound.
findings.caller: Native Q2 module message/sound imports -> guest_native_q2_services.c:195/203 and :273/280 -> qa_application_network_q2_unicast (network_q2_hooks.c:445) -> installed frontend host unicast callback (network_q2_host.c:91) -> qa_q2_unicast_check/reserve/remember. The constructor (network_q2_host.c:373) allocates only the owner and does not prepare claim storage, so first or larger live event groups grow here.
findings.replacement: Keep the typed qa_q2_unicast_claim and connection/source/frame retirement semantics, but prepare claim payload storage from the shared qa_pool/qa_arena at load/bind. Use the common keyed-index mechanism for the source/frame/client/key lookup instead of a new private index. Save capture/restore allocations are cold and are not this finding. Size against actual admitted connection/source and event-memory bounds, not a guessed smaller claim cap.
findings.semantics: One native group event must be sent once to the canonical client even when it targets several local seats. Preserve connection epoch, map revision, native source frame/time, duplicate key and retirement on client/source/domain changes; failed reservations cannot discard already remembered live claims.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Each live Unified handshake exchange creates and destroys heap-backed typed documents and an owned wire buffer, despite the payload having a fixed bounded record layout.
findings.caller: Physical packet -> frontend_network_intake/qa_network_events_collect -> qa_sys_event dispatch -> network_dispatch -> qa_network_receive -> connectionless (frontend/network.c:1367, or local client:543) -> frontend_network_unified_receive -> qa_unified_bootstrap_receive -> qa_unified_handshake_read. Replies/retries call send_handshake -> qa_unified_handshake_write. Read allocates a temporary document via typed_document; write allocates that document and a growing builder, then frees both.
findings.replacement: Use the existing qa_unified_handshake_layout and qa_unified_record_delta_decode/write directly with caller-owned qa_unified_handshake and a fixed bootstrap-owned or stack wire buffer; keep one codec and delete the handshake's temporary document round trip. This does not require another allocator or reader.
findings.semantics: Keep QUHS envelope, enum/nonce/token field layout, exact token bytes, external length/domain checks, address/challenge matching, retry order and send behavior. This finding concerns live connectionless processing/retries, not cold bootstrap/session constructors.
findings.verification: Live unified handshake reads the existing bounded layout and writes caller-owned storage, without temporary documents. Existing document decode delegates it; core checks compare wire bytes and failure output behavior. Matching normal build and seven core suites passed; no live or performance claim.

findings.summary: The shipped Unified receive path decodes and validates the same datagram three times and contains three copies of the token-mismatch loop.
findings.caller: Queued physical event -> frontend_network_receive -> network_dispatch -> qa_network_receive. Its peer matching calls qa_unified_session_peer_matches (decode/token); target->ops.receive invokes receive_peer (decode/token/limits); receive_peer invokes qa_unified_channel_receive_buffered (decode/token/limits again) before the actual ACK/fragment processing.
findings.replacement: Retain one parsed/authenticated qa_unified_packet view for this delivery and pass it to channel processing; keep the standalone byte boundary as the single qa_unified_packet_decode implementation. Share the token comparison/admission operation instead of the three handwritten XOR loops. Endpoint dispatch remains a protocol/client routing operation.
findings.semantics: Do not remove external authentication, endpoint matching, packet-kind/header/fragment checks or configured channel limits. Preserve silent discard of invalid or foreign packets, ACK ordering, reliable dependencies, source timestamps and exact existing wire widths. No content hashing is involved.
findings.verification: Source callers migrated and replaced paths deleted; matching normal production build and seven core suites passed. No live or performance claim.

findings.summary: The typed per-frame snapshot still stores authored attachment/anchor paths and tags, weapon identity and prediction-provider identities as copied text instead of retained name IDs.
findings.caller: frontend_network_publish -> frontend_network_unified_publish -> application_unified_server_publish -> application_unified_output_acquire builds visual and prediction cuts. unified_presentations copies admission-time equipment path/tag text each frame; unified_prediction copies provider instance names. QA_UNIFIED_FIELD_STRING equality uses strcmp and decode clones each changed/unchanged string into frame storage. The receiving authored Q3 weapon path calls qa_q3_register_model by anchor/attachment text during scene submission; regular model content/path and active_weapon already use NAME fields.
findings.replacement: Bind authored names to the existing shared qa_string_id table at equipment/recipe admission and use QA_UNIFIED_FIELD_NAME in the internal snapshot, matching the existing model content/path/provider and active_weapon fields. Resolve authored model handles/tag bindings when the authored selection changes and reuse during draw. Remove fields if their only uses are producer plus serialization (the prediction arsenal_provider/character_provider and model weapon_item have no semantic readers found in the complete source search).
findings.semantics: Retain original authored attachment order, anchor offsets/FOV rules, ownership selection and source model limits. UTF-8 names may still be spelled at the wire/module boundary using the same field encoding; do not treat dynamic display labels or print text as identities. Leases already avoid general-heap growth here; the gap is name-primitive adoption and repeated copying/lookup.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Composition sorting has a private UTF-8 scalar decoder alongside the shared text primitive.
findings.caller: Recipe publish/import/save boundary -> qa_unified_composition_create -> qa_unified_canonical -> qsort(compare_members) -> next_unit. next_unit decodes UTF-8 bytes manually before producing UTF-16 units; common qa_utf8_next already owns scalar iteration. This is cold composition canonicalization, not a per-frame cost.
findings.replacement: Use qa_utf8_next for scalar decoding, retain the small UTF-16-unit ordering adapter and pending low surrogate needed by this external canonical-order contract, and delete the duplicate UTF-8 decoding logic.
findings.semantics: JSON input has already been validated; preserve UTF-16 key ordering, supplementary-before-BMP ordering and duplicate-key ordinal policy. Do not replace that specific ordering with Unicode scalar order.
findings.verification: Source callers migrated and replaced paths deleted; matching normal production build and seven core suites passed. No live or performance claim.

findings.summary: API2023 native Q2 keyed unicast grows a private heap array during module execution instead of using load-sized common storage.
findings.caller: Shipped Q2 HOST construction calls qa_q2_unicast_cache_create at frontend/network_q2_host.c:373, which allocates the owner but leaves row capacity zero. During an API2023 game import, native_host/q2.c:547-549 dispatches gi.unicast to native_host_message_send; message.c:205-206 carries its key flags, then message.c:222-223 invokes the engine message callback installed at guest_native_q2_services.c:316. native_q2_delivery.c:321-322 captures the API2023 unicast dupe_key. guest_native_q2_services.c:194-196 calls qa_application_network_q2_unicast before event publication; network_q2_hooks.c:464-467 builds the live frame/client claim and calls the HOST hook. network_q2_host.c:103-104 invokes qa_q2_unicast_reserve, whose first or larger keyed workload reallocates rows at unicast.c:45. Successful publication remembers the key at services.c:203-204 and unicast.c:62-63. The local-sound keyed delivery path at services.c:272-281 uses the same cache. This is in-module runtime growth, not the cold owner allocation or cold save-capture allocation.
findings.replacement: Prepare the needed claim storage through the existing common qa_pool/qa_arena at Q2 HOST load/admission, with a load-sized claim budget and explicit backpressure before publication. The APIs are already present in include/qa/pool.h:22-35; no second cache-specific allocator is needed. Keep the pure duplicate lookup and receipt-after-publication ordering, but remove runtime realloc from reserve/remember.
findings.semantics: Preserve Q2 rerelease client-group duplicate suppression keyed by client id, connection epoch, source, map revision, source frame/time and key. Remember only accepted Source publication; remove old-frame and disconnected/retired-source claims. API3 messages legitimately have key zero and do not use this path. The API2023 dupe key is a guest/protocol requirement and must remain; it is not an unwanted hash.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Q2 rerelease HUD retirement re-copies admitted provider identity into per-retirement heap objects and compares it by string instead of retaining the delivered interned ids and common storage.
findings.caller: Shipped unified presentation installs its event consumer callbacks at remote_unified_presentation.c:381-387. An admitted OWNER event is delivered through remote_unified_events.c:543, then presentation.c:150-154 calls frontend_unified_q2_owner_retire, which invokes the RR HUD retirement at remote_unified_q2.c:335-336. RR retirement checks string equality at hud.c:572 and allocates a separate rr_retired plus provider copy at hud.c:573-578; that list survives until HUD destruction. Subsequent RR presentation events parse row->owner.provider into rr_record at hud.c:153 and, at hud.c:415, consult the list using strcmp at hud.c:226. Owner cleanup also uses strcmp at hud.c:563. The event receiver already interns OWNER payload providers at remote_unified_events.c:343 into row->payload_owner_id, and normal presentation rows carry row->owner_provider_id. The parent Q2 presentation already uses those ids for its load-sized activation pool at remote_unified_q2.c:229-239 and :338; its activations are released on retirement (:371-373), so they are not themselves a substitute for the RR tombstone lifetime.
findings.replacement: Store qa_string_id plus generation for RR records and retirement tombstones, using row->owner_provider_id and row->payload_owner_id directly; prepare tombstone backing through the existing common qa_pool/qa_arena at HUD construction instead of calloc/malloc per owner retirement. Share the owner-lifetime predicate with the existing event component registry only where its lifetime coverage is equivalent; otherwise keep the necessary tombstone policy with common identity/storage primitives. hud.c:508-513 already demonstrates that constructor using the common sealed pool backing.
findings.semantics: Preserve retirement of every matching RR POI/bar/damage/objective/help record and rejection of late events for the retired provider generation. Distinguish generation changes and preserve normal refresh/admission events. This is a final event delivery consumer, so it is not an event-ring producer bypass. A tombstone lifetime is intentional policy; string-copy identity and per-retirement heap storage are the foundation-adoption gaps.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: The enabled live profiler bypasses retained names and load-sized storage: each frame scope mallocs its label and scans totals with strcmp, and first/deeper scopes grow private arrays during play.
findings.caller: The shipped timers on console command enters tools_timer_command (src/tools/profiler.c:250) -> qa_profiler_enable. frontend_step (frame.c:816 onward) repeatedly calls qa_profiler_push/pop for source maintenance, network, application, presentation and audio; frontend_frame_present adds renderer/present scopes. When enabled, push always calls tools_copy, which mallocs; pop scans totals by label and frees that copy after the first call. qa_profiler_stamp also allocates labels for the live stamp ring. Disabled profiling does not take this allocating path.
findings.replacement: Resolve timer labels once to retained qa_string_id or a stable timer handle, index totals directly by that handle, and load-size stack/totals/stamp records with the existing qa_pool/qa_arena primitives. Console-created stamp labels can be interned at command admission, with the fixed stamp ring retaining ids instead of owned copies.
findings.semantics: Keep optional profiling, nested elapsed/self-time accounting, deferred mode changes while a scope is active, bounded stamp-ring order and human-readable report labels. This is an optional live instrumentation adoption gap, not evidence that ordinary disabled frames allocate.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Runtime world text still has a heap-grown font store outside the event-page retention path; native Q2 GAME Draw_WorldText imports write directly into it, while QC debug text copies already-admitted payloads into the same private heap store.
findings.caller: A live API2023 native Q2 game module Draw_WorldText import reaches native_host_q2_import -> q2_application (compat/native_host/q2.c:441,583) -> the frontend_native_q2_services callback -> application_import_body slots 59/60 -> world_text -> qa_font_world_store_submit. There is no event-ring admission in this producer chain. frontend_native_q2_world_text snapshots the private store for each presentation. Separately, frontend QC rerelease event_body handles QA_QC_BUILTIN_EX_DRAW_WORLDTEXT and calls that store after reading the admitted builtin event. submit mallocs every nonempty text, reallocs the entry array on growth, and snapshot/pruning frees runtime payloads.
findings.replacement: Use one retained world-text representation over the existing application output ring pages and leases (application_unified_world_text_append/publish); add native Q2 import and QC debug-event adapters to that representation. Font drawing should consume admitted retained records or shared fixed-pool storage rather than create a second growable payload lifetime. The QC function is a delivery consumer, so its issue is the secondary heap retention, not producer admission.
findings.semantics: Preserve native Q2 fixed versus billboard orientation, source encoding conversion, font selection, content owner, colour, depth-test and distance culling; preserve source-clock lifetime and zero-lifetime text visible for one presentation frame across every seat. Several store instances currently use one font implementation: the finding is runtime storage/event adoption, not merely multiple objects.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Registered Q3 guest Cvar_Update still reroutes a retained handle by its copied name and compares copied names/values on every update, maintaining a separate heap-owned change mirror instead of relying on the shared canonical handle and revision.
findings.caller: frontend_source_present -> qa_application_present -> q3g_call(command 3, CGAME draw) -> native/QVM host syscall dispatch -> cvars_selected trap 4 (or UI 51) -> update -> update_fields -> routed_view for every registered negative guest token. routed_view resolves namespace, calls access_name with the retained string, then reads the handle, strcmp-checks its name and old value, and allocates a new old-value copy whenever first read/changed. CGAME status-cache refresh after draw invokes update_fields again. This route does not call qa_cvars_find for every update: the concrete gap is repeated string routing/comparison and the private mirror, not a claimed name-table search.
findings.replacement: Bind each guest token once to the common qa_cvar_handle and its view/role data; rebind it only at an actual role/store publication boundary. Read with qa_cvars_read or the existing prepared handle reader, use common modification/role revision for change detection, and store the cg_drawStatus classification as a registration-time flag. Keep any necessary guest-visible revision translation as numeric adapter state without owned name/value copies.
findings.semantics: Preserve the exact 272-byte vmCvar ABI, signed guest tokens and MAX_CVARS/MAX_CVAR_VALUE_STRING limits, guest defaults/aliases and per-seat views, and cg_drawStatus suppression/restoration across the selected HUD. Production view registries already share one underlying cvar store; this finding does not claim independent cvar tables.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Q3 live scene submission retains a second heap-grown scene alongside the existing fixed scene bank, and copies the bank back into it before rendering.
findings.caller: Unified Q3 character_part -> qa_q3_presentation_entity -> q3p_reserve realloc when the backend has no source_state; Unified backend_read creates precisely that backend. Original/QVM source.c backend supplies source_state, but qa_q3_presentation_render -> source_scene_snapshot copies entities/polygons/vertices/lights into the same heap-grown private arrays. Portal storage also grows during render.
findings.replacement: Use one load-sized scene-bank storage primitive for all backends, with bounded frame-arena conversion scratch where renderer vertices differ. Delete private growable entity/poly/light ownership and q3p_reserve on the play path.
findings.semantics: Keep ClearScene and first-scene membership, original Q3 scene admission limits, per-cell asset namespace custody, vertex colour conversion, and portal-view temporary mutation lifetime. Cold asset admission allocation is not the finding.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: CPU draw-time scratch still privately allocates/grows brush contexts, clipping buffers, surface/edge/span lists and transformed vertices.
findings.caller: CPU renderer draw command at renderer.c:1006 -> cpu_draw_queued -> cpu_draw_impl -> cpu_brush_draw_queued; CPU brush flush -> generate_spans. Non-brush draws call transform, which reallocs renderer->vertices when the reached mesh is larger. Brush contexts are created only when encountered during draw, and further contexts are created while earlier contexts remain queued.
findings.replacement: Reserve caller-owned common qa_arena/qa_pool storage during load, with distinct leases for queued contexts until raster retirement; reuse fixed transformed-vertex storage. The raster batch itself already demonstrates sealed qa_arena and qa_jobs adoption.
findings.semantics: Preserve queued worker lifetimes and pinned surface-cache entries, multiple views/seats, rounding-mode separation, clipping capacity, and generic fallback for unsupported/nonplanar brushes. Do not reset storage before queued rows retire or reduce scene capacity.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Q3 effect delivery invokes whole-application event retirement once per effect and privately repeats raw ring traversal.
findings.caller: Native, remote and compiled Q3 frame event production -> event_publish commits QA_APPLICATION_EVENT_Q3_EFFECT -> q3n_events_deliver. Every matching effect calls qa_application_events_consumed, whose implementation scans component/subscriber cursors and releases/retire records. This is the ring final consumer, not a producer bypass.
findings.replacement: Advance this reader cursor per successful effect and perform retirement once at the delivery boundary. Provide/use one raw-record iterator with kind filtering rather than per-consumer read/filter loops; the current view-range iterator only covers unified projection records.
findings.semantics: Failed later effects must not replay effects already delivered; preserve actor-generation/recipient filtering, predicted entities, source sound origins and oldest-live cursor retirement. Ring records remain immutable.
findings.verification: Raw-record kind-mask iteration replaces the named event walks; Q3 effects retire once at the batch boundary and retain successful-prefix/error retry semantics. Matching normal build and seven core suites passed; no live or performance claim.

findings.summary: Completed Q3 frame checks reconstruct and parse serverinfo repeatedly inside individual HUD glyph, entity and effect operations.
findings.caller: Remote Q3 frame.c/native draw -> HUD text/pictures -> q3nh_pixels -> q3nh_current -> q3ne_current/q3n_frame_current -> q3n_remote_frame_current -> q3n_remote_source_current -> q3n_remote_source_read. The final read walks SERVERINFO for g_gametype/sv_maxclients/dmflags and reparses level-start configstring. Team Arena q3nm_result similarly rechecks the whole source/recipient tuple after each drawing adapter; local checks reread native client context.
findings.replacement: Capture the typed presentation frame once at frame/externally reentrant boundaries; retain parsed serverinfo by config revision and use captured fields internally. Keep one source/recipient generation comparison at mutation boundaries instead of read/parse/revalidate per glyph or entity.
findings.semantics: Preserve published snapshot identity and command ordering, map restart/generation changes, remote versus compiled source ownership and callback-driven retirement. Do not silently substitute a different frame or relax external ABI bounds.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Selected Q3 weapon drawing converts retained handles back to paths and revalidates the entire admitted media inventory on each read; the authored variant duplicates the same machinery.
findings.caller: Per-frame equipment Q3 draw_output reads q3n_selected_media; source-style output reads it again. read -> valid walks all 14 weapon rows, reconstructs barrel/flash/hand paths and resolves q3p_find_name for each model/shader. Authored equipment draw invokes q3n_selected_authored_read -> an equivalent path/handle/source validator over attachments.
findings.replacement: Validate and bind model/shader/animation custody once during admission/rebind. Read selected row through retained handles and generation/custody already held by assets; share one admission routine for built-in and authored rows and delete play-time name reconstruction/full inventory validation.
findings.semantics: Preserve optional absent barrel/flash, required gun/hands and shotgun hand fallback, asset namespaces across simultaneous mods, animation source lifetime, and authored attachment counts. This finding concerns live read-time reproof, not cold asset loading.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Q3 animation.cfg is decoded independently in client-info and selected-equipment code despite an existing common model decoder.
findings.caller: Player configstring registration -> client_info register_model -> animation -> parse_animation. Selected equipment media admission -> selected_media animation -> q3n_selected_animation_parse. qa_player_animation_load already implements the same animation.cfg header, 31 source rows, leg-offset correction and generated rows in the one model reader.
findings.replacement: Use the one qa_player_animation_load decoder for both callers, preserving original numeric and diagnostic semantics in that decoder; caller adapters may decide fallback versus hard admission failure. Delete the private token/parser/row loops.
findings.semantics: Keep footsteps/sex/head offset/fixed legs/torso, reversed animations, optional Team Arena gesture rows falling back to torso gesture, leg-frame offset, generated backwards/flag rows, 19,998-byte original admission limit, and caller-specific missing-file fallback. Existing common decoder differs on overflow/rounding; reconcile original rules rather than blindly swap.
findings.verification: One model animation.cfg decoder serves native client-info and selected equipment; private lexers, numeric and row loops are deleted. Source COM grammar, 31 records, optional Team Arena fallback rows, leg offsets, generated rows and caller fallback/strict policies remain. The existing number parser carries original bytecode precision as data; FPS division now follows source binary32 rules. Existing model tests cover metadata, reverse/negative loops, zero FPS, optional rows and unchanged output on incomplete records. Normal production build and seven core suites passed; no live model or performance claim.

findings.summary: Q3 HUD and pickup effects still resolve fixed item media by path on every draw/event instead of the retained item media rows; attacker name is reparsed from configstring.
findings.caller: Native/remote/compiled Q3 HUD -> team_overlay/powerups or mission item_picture -> item-table scan and qa_q3_register_shader(item->icon). Q3 pickup ring delivery -> pickup -> qa_q3_register_sound(item->sound). media item_now already retains icon and item_sounds retains pickup_sound. Upper attacker HUD parses configstring n despite q3n_client_info.name already being bound.
findings.replacement: Use retained indexed item/media rows and client-info name. Bind required mip/no-mip icon variants during item admission, and retain pickup sound handles. Resolve tag-to-item once in the shared item registry instead of repeated item-table scans.
findings.semantics: Keep source distinctions between powerup/global pickup sounds and local generic health sound, Team Arena persistent-powerup sounds, HUD icon sampling variants (some callers request mipmapped, others no-mip), attacker timeout and per-seat player name.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Q3 presentation still carries several private float-to-int and decimal-integer implementations rather than the common numeric primitives.
findings.caller: Native/remote/compiled presentation invokes integer(float) in packet interpolation, pose/animation, weapon presentation, particles and HUD/effects. Remote frame and server-command parsing independently repeat signed decimal accumulation and bit reinterpretation. Float casts match qa_source_float_to_i32, already provided by core/number.c:54.
findings.replacement: Replace private float conversion with qa_source_float_to_i32. Centralize decimal integer parsing and wrapped 32-bit arithmetic in the one core number implementation (a precise wrapped integer primitive is currently missing), then remove word/sum/difference/parser copies.
findings.semantics: Keep native/QVM binary32 conversion semantics (INT32_MIN for NaN/out of range, truncation otherwise), deliberate 32-bit wrap for original protocol/VM time arithmetic, signed-byte whitespace and prefix parsing. Do not replace integer accumulation with floating-point parsing or saturating conversion.
findings.verification: Private presentation float/decimal conversion and wrapped arithmetic replaced by common numeric primitives; all scoped callers migrated and old symbols deleted. Matching normal build and seven existing core suites passed, including signed wrap boundary cases. No live presentation or performance claim.

findings.summary: Q3 item and attachment placement still expands common axis/normalization operations by hand, and selected equipment has a second tag-composition routine.
findings.caller: Item packet submission expands midpoint-to-parent axes manually; player body and native weapon attach through q3n_attach; selected built-in/authored equipment attaches through selected_attach. Both sample qa_q3_presentation_tag and combine parent/tag/child axes, while selected adds required-tag and pose-field behavior. Per-frame player pose manually computes length/inverse and scales velocity.
findings.replacement: Use qa_axis_from_local and qa_vec_normalize_length, and one tag-attachment primitive with explicit required/optional, rotated and field-copy semantics. Delete duplicated composition loops; callers retain original game placement/flags.
findings.semantics: Preserve scalar operation order where original rounding matters, optional missing tags, required tag_weapon failure at content admission, rotated child axes versus unrotated inheritance, back_lerp, old_origin and lighting_origin differences. These are caller rule data, not grounds for two geometry-composition implementations.
findings.verification: One tag attachment body replaces native/selected duplicates with explicit arithmetic, field and missing-tag policies. All seventeen callers migrated; item axes and pose normalization use shared math. Matching normal production build and seven existing core suites passed; no live visual comparison or performance claim.

findings.summary: Q3 presentation has its own trajectory position/velocity evaluator while gameplay already uses the shared trajectory primitive.
findings.caller: Native/remote/compiled Q3 packet interpolation, predicted player placement, weapon trails and local fragment movement call q3n_trajectory/q3n_trajectory_delta. Gameplay movers, items and missiles already call qa_trajectory_position/qa_trajectory_velocity on the same six Q3 trajectory rules.
findings.replacement: Keep one evaluator in the common physics trajectory primitive; presentation may only convert qa_q3_trajectory ABI fields to qa_trajectory. Reconcile arithmetic with original Q3 and remove the presentation evaluator and its private wrapped-time helpers.
findings.semantics: Preserve stationary/interpolate/linear/linear-stop/sine/gravity rules, 32-bit wrapped elapsed/end time, fixed Q3 gravity 800 independent of selected world gravity, half-amplitude sine velocity and linear-stop boundary. Current evaluators differ in binary32 versus double intermediate milliseconds/sin/gravity; unify after preserving the required original numerical behavior, not a blind redirect.
findings.verification: Presentation converts ABI fields and delegates one qsrc-derived trajectory implementation. Core checks cover wrapped stop boundaries, gravity, milliseconds, half-amplitude sine velocity and invalid-output preservation. Matching normal build and seven core suites passed; no live or performance claim.

findings.summary: Native and received Q3 model/sound configstring changes duplicate the same heap-copy/register/revalidate operation during server-command delivery.
findings.caller: Live Q3 reliable cs command -> server_commands config_modified -> native, remote or compiled media configstring_changed. Both implementations malloc and copy the reached model/sound row, register it, compare the same revision/text, update the same observed slot and free; these changes can arrive during play, beyond initial media admission.
findings.replacement: Use one media-row change routine with a source-reader adapter. Borrow immutable ring-leased text where guaranteed, otherwise use common load-sized command scratch with correct nested lifetime instead of per-message malloc/free. Retain model/sound handles and slot revisions once after successful admission.
findings.semantics: Preserve 32..287 model and 288..543 sound slot mapping, sexed * sound handling, native reached-command sequence and source revision at externally reentrant registration boundaries. Asset registration may invoke callbacks: a borrowed pointer must remain leased or be copied into nested-safe scratch until registration finishes. Cold asset decoder allocation itself is not this finding.
findings.verification: One native/remote/compiled media-row updater uses the existing command-local stable snapshot. Reached revision/sequence and reentrant registration retained. Matching normal build and seven core suites; no live asset claim.

findings.summary: Live effect/world code still implements vector rotation, perpendicular-vector selection, portal-axis remapping and transformed bounds outside the common math layer.
findings.caller: qa_frontend_step -> frontend_present -> scene_build. Live Q2 beams reach qa_scene_model_submit -> qa_scene_beam (models.c:1550) and frontend_q2_entity_effects/remote_q2_effects reach the same beam builder; Q3 ref rails reach presentation/q3/render.c:784 -> qa_scene_rail_geometry. Q3 portal rendering reaches presentation/q3/render.c:1385 -> qa_scene_world_portal_view -> qa_scene_portal_view. Inline models reach frontend/visuals.c:1347/1440 -> qa_scene_world_submit_model -> qaw_transformed_bounds.
findings.replacement: Use qa_vec_perpendicular, qa_vec_rotate_around and qa_axis_remap from core/math.c and qa/math.h, and qa_model_transform_bounds from formats/model/transform.c. Add the missing direction-only scene-matrix operation to the shared scene-math implementation rather than keeping q3.c matrix_vector. Where currently different round-off/order is intentional, encode that as data in the single math primitive.
findings.semantics: Preserve source rotation handedness, tie-breaking, float-vs-double conversion points, non-normalized axes, portal/mirror clipping, and the exact original beam/rail/sky appearance; Rodrigues and the existing matrix rotation are not automatically bit-identical.
findings.verification: Named source callers migrated and replaced implementation deleted; matching normal production build and seven core suites passed. No live, performance or whole-frame allocation claim.

findings.summary: Renderer resource lookup has an independent hash-index implementation and CPU skin deduplication implements another probing table instead of using the common index primitive.
findings.caller: frontend_frame_present -> qa_gl_execute -> draw_scene/gl_texture_get/gl_mesh_bind -> render_resource_get/reserve; qa_cpu_execute -> skin_frame_prepare -> skin_slot and cpu_brush_draw_queued -> cpu_surface_cache_prepare -> render_resource_get. The private table is shared by CPU and GL, but duplicates the engine's general index reserve/find/remove machinery.
findings.replacement: Use the common qa_id_index implementation, extended with a full-width composite-key facility or dense admitted handles as necessary. Keep one core index implementation; preserve the original identity/revision/owner tuple and do not truncate uint64 identities or pointer owners to qa_string_id.
findings.semantics: These hashes are permitted bucket hashes, not content fingerprints. Exact full-key equality, multiple resource owners, revisions, removal after frame leases and Source/GPU texture correspondence must remain intact.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Normal renderer execution still grows heap-backed scratch on new frame high-water marks, and Source overdraw allocates a framebuffer-sized array on every enabled frame.
findings.caller: qa_frontend_step frame.c:1011 -> frontend_present -> frontend_frame_present presentation.c:183-184 -> qa_cpu_execute/qa_gl_execute. CPU execute_commands:1030 calls skin_frame_prepare:915/929 -> skin_jobs_reserve/skin_transient_reserve. GL execute_commands:1295 calls gl_skeletal_frame; DRAW -> world_draw_run:1137 -> gl_world_group_prepare:1402 -> world_index_reserve and skeletal fallback; PARTICLES:1318 -> gl_particles_prepare; OUTPUT_DOMAIN:1359 (CPU:1141) -> qa_output_domains_assign. qa_gl_swap -> source_frame overdraw readback allocates/frees every frame when enabled.
findings.replacement: Use the existing sealed qa_scene_frame storage/qa_pool primitive for frame-lifetime arrays, or load-admitted renderer pools sized from admitted geometry/particle/view capacities for retained arrays. Reserve resources at admission, not during execute; retain a framebuffer-sized diagnostic buffer through resize. Delete these live malloc/realloc branches.
findings.semantics: Some allocations happen on first use or a later larger visible batch, not every stable frame. Preserve unlimited-to-admitted capacity, all seats, combined providers, skeletal rounding fallback, particle geometry, output-domain overlay/stereo ordering, and diagnostic readback. Do not invent a smaller cap or silently drop excess draws.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Legacy world submission owns a heap-resized lightstyle snapshot even though the styles are an input to a frame.
findings.caller: frontend legacy scene -> qa_scene_world_submit -> world_submit:1649 -> qawl_light_styles; every inline legacy brush submission calls it again at world_submit_model:1759. Changing style_count allocates a replacement and frees the old snapshot inside submission; stable count still copies it for each world/model call.
findings.replacement: Keep sampled style data in one frame-owned arena snapshot or load-sized shared lightstyle storage and pass the captured span through lighting calls. Use the existing qa_lightstyles owner for the retained patterns; remove the render-world malloc/free snapshot path.
findings.semantics: Preserve Q1 float light values, Q2 RGB styles, extended style counts, per-view/native-timeline samples and lightmap dirty-style comparisons. Do not replace rerelease/extension ranges with a stock 64-entry cap or borrow mutable data past its lifetime.
findings.verification: Legacy numeric style snapshots allocate once from actual face/grid references. Full supplied spans remain validated, including unreachable suffixes; core checks cover extended indices, grid-only styles and shrink/re-expand. Last-submission sampling remains world-owned. Matching normal build and seven core suites passed; no live or performance claim.

findings.summary: Model shader/image binding performs a private linked-list search on each mesh draw and can register/allocate a binding from inside submission.
findings.caller: Q3 presentation/q3/render.c:485/563 sets input.material_library, then qa_scene_model_submit -> model_submit mesh loop -> select_image:853/877 -> scene_model_material. A custom skin without a material-library binding reaches scene_model_external_id:857. Unified presentation similarly supplies model materials at remote_unified_render.c:247.
findings.replacement: Bind admitted material/image handles once per model/provider/library generation using qa_id_index keyed by the existing shader ID and exact library identity. Keep first registration in the content admission phase and make select_image an indexed read. Delete scene_model_resource_binding list searches and per-draw registration allocation.
findings.semantics: Different providers/libraries and custom skins must remain distinct; retain their material/image leases and invalidate only on actual policy/provider rebind. Source default-shader fallback and MD3/MD4 behavior must survive.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Generic cross-game image mapping and image-to-request reads still scan resource lists/cache arrays on live material-stage submission.
findings.caller: qa_material_submit -> texture material/submit.c:131 -> frontend generic_recipient_image -> qa_scene_image_generic_variant. Each Source-Q3 image displayed by a generic recipient scans cache entries and all owned images before returning an existing variant. Source variant admission also calls qa_scene_image_request_read:2526 and linearly scans the image cache. The Source-recipient path has a generation correspondence fast path at resources.c:2643; that path is not being claimed as an unconditional per-stage scan.
findings.replacement: Use the existing qa_id_index/request index and admitted image handles for reverse image-to-recipe lookup and exact source-image/mipmap/policy-generation variant lookup. Resolve animation-parent correspondence at admission. Delete the duplicate image/list scans.
findings.semantics: Preserve first-recipient canonical correspondence, retained original recipe, mip/picmip policy, animation frames, VFS/policy revisions and mixed Q3-material rendering in Q1/Q2 views. Bucket lookup is allowed; no fingerprint of image pixels/content.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Every dirty Q3 cinematic upload creates and copies a new heap-owned scene image version on the frame path.
findings.caller: Live shader movie -> frontend_material_movies_frontend_resolve -> frontend_material_movies_resolve:526 -> qa_q3_cinematic_shader_resolve:666 -> upload -> qa_scene_image_source_scratch_version -> qa_scene_image_create. The same upload helper is used for cinematic UI drawing. Image creation callocs owner/level descriptors, mallocs lineage and pixel storage, copies pixels, then frees the newly created lineage and substitutes the scratch lineage.
findings.replacement: Use one load-sized common pool for cinematic image-version descriptors and pixel blocks, or the existing scene streaming-image primitive where ordering permits. Retire versions after their frame leases rather than allocating/freeing one per decoded picture. Keep the one scene image reader/owner.
findings.semantics: A new version cannot simply overwrite a previously leased version: preserve dirty/redefine behavior, decoder dimensions, stable scratch identity plus revision, UI/shader usage, queued draw lifetimes and asynchronous CPU/GPU consumers. Reserve the existing cinematic-slot capacities at load; no frame dropping or arbitrary new truncation.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Image deduplication writes a private frame visit epoch into resource objects instead of using caller-owned qa_stamp_set scratch.
findings.caller: All admitted scene draws -> qa_scene_frame_emit -> pin (frame.c:328/329); image/stream/particle/target commands call the same pin helper at :350-373. pin casts an immutable qa_scene_image to owned_image and writes frame_pin_epoch; qa_scene_frame_reset resets its own epoch and releases the retained array.
findings.replacement: Use one caller-owned qa_stamp_set plus stable admitted image-slot lookup in frame storage. Remove frame_pin_epoch from loaded image/resource state and retire only the frame's retained references on reset.
findings.semantics: Keep deduplication and reference balancing for images shared by multiple scene frames/owners, Source prefixes and image revisions. Do not truncate the 64-bit scene identity to a stamp index; resolve a stable slot. This is a storage/adoption finding, not a claim of a demonstrated race.
findings.verification: One frame-owned common ID index pins immutable images by their full creation serial. Index membership supplies the visit test; a second stamp store would duplicate it. Core checks interleaved frames, reset/re-admission and independent retained lifetimes. No whole-frame allocation or timing claim.

findings.summary: Visibility and Q1 mirror rendering still have independent BSP traversal engines beside the shared read-only geometry walkers.
findings.caller: Every world view -> qa_scene_world_source_prepare_view/world_submit/qa_scene_world_portal_view -> world_visible. Enabled Q1 mirrors reach frontend_legacy_scene:502 -> qa_scene_world_q1_mirror -> another private near/faces/far BSP walk. Marks and point-light sampling already use shared geometry walks; these two rendering traversals do not.
findings.replacement: Expose the missing read-only BSP tree visitor from the common collision/geometry query layer with caller-owned scratch and caller-supplied pruning/order/payload data; migrate visibility and mirror traversal to it and delete the private traversal engines. qa_collision_walk_leaves already owns the shared tree-box walk but does not yet supply all required rendering callbacks.
findings.semantics: Keep Q1 near-face-far order and mirror texture-chain head selection; Q2/Q3 PVS/area exclusion, Q3 four-plane culling, per-node dynamic-light masks, multiple-parent topology and render leaf 0 semantics must remain caller rule data. Do not replace them blindly with a collision box query or change original visual ordering.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Several immutable render-name decisions are still rediscovered during draw/view generation rather than bound at admission.
findings.caller: World Q3 submission -> qaw_submit_q3 sets source_default_material by qa_material_find("*default") per submitted surface, normalizing and comparing text despite qa_material_library_builtin. Each raw Q1 surface draw -> animated_texture reclassifies '+'/'A' texture-name bytes; textures.c:106 already classifies animation cycles at admission. Enabled Q1 mirror preparation rescans every texture name each view.
findings.replacement: Use qa_material_library_builtin(QA_MATERIAL_BUILTIN_DEFAULT) and retain animation-cycle/mirror texture handles or typed flags during qawl_textures_build. Delete hot text classifications and name lookups.
findings.semantics: Retain policy-source builtin inheritance, Q1 normal/alternate animation timing and phase rounding, and the original last matching window02_1 mirror-texture selection. Names remain available for diagnostics/admission only.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Classic Q1 sky-flat color is recomputed by scanning every overlay texel on every view.
findings.caller: frontend_legacy_scene scene():286-287 -> qa_scene_world_q1_sky_begin. It scans texture entries for the last sky pair and then sums every opaque foreground RGBA texel before collecting/drawing sky polygons; this repeats per seat/mirror/view.
findings.replacement: Retain the selected sky-layer handles and exact opaque-foreground average as immutable admission metadata when qawl_textures_build/split_sky creates the shared image layers, and refresh it only on real image-policy rebind. View generation should read the retained metadata.
findings.semantics: Keep the original last-admitted sky choice, transparency mask, Quake64 behavior and fog color override. resources.c:2245 computes a BACK-layer average for transparent edge fill; that is not the same foreground average and cannot be substituted.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: The same generic gamma-table capability is implemented separately in CPU runtime, CPU candidate preparation and GL output.
findings.caller: frontend_frame_present reads the common r_gamma handle then calls qa_cpu_set_gamma/qa_gl_set_gamma. CPU surface/gamma candidate preparation repeats the CPU table formula; GL output/candidate preparation calls a separate gl_gamma_table using powf/floorf rather than CPU pow/floor.
findings.replacement: Use one shared gamma-table builder, called by active output and candidate preparation. If source-compatible precision requires distinct evaluation policies, make the policy explicit data in that one implementation; leave backend upload/compositing in CPU/GL.
findings.semantics: Preserve byte rounding, gamma==1 identity, source-domain gamma bypass, alpha, stereo surfaces and source-compatible software/GL looks. CPU and GL current formulas are not assumed bit-identical.
findings.verification: CPU and GL output use one gamma-table builder with explicit original arithmetic policies. Source-palette/overbright behavior is unchanged; no pixel or timing claim. Matching normal build and seven core suites passed; no live or performance claim.

findings.summary: An uncalled shadow-caster pipeline still fingerprints transformed model content and retains private caster identities.
findings.caller: No shipped callers exist for qa_scene_model_shadow_caster, qa_scene_world_shadow_caster, qa_scene_shadows_create or qa_scene_shadows_prepare_options in this immutable src tree. Only definitions, public declarations and the internal prepare wrapper remain. If invoked, caster revision is FNV over transformed vertices/indices, and caster identity is a per-model entity linked list.
findings.replacement: Delete the unreachable shadow pipeline and its declarations/identity storage, or migrate any intentionally retained SDK capability to stable actor/resource IDs plus actual geometry/pose generation counters before enabling it. Use shared scene-matrix math instead of the private shadow multiply.
findings.semantics: This is dormant cleanup and a confirmed prohibited content-fingerprint site, not live per-frame CPU usage. No SHA is involved. If the SDK capability is intentionally retained, preserve its double accumulation through an explicit shared math rule and stable lease lifetimes.
findings.verification: Dormant model fingerprint/caster/atlas paths are deleted. Original reached planar and stencil shadow paths and reserved identity slot remain. Matching normal build and seven core suites passed; no live or performance claim.

findings.summary: Builtin actor snapshots keep a second growable nested buffer pool and copy shared world snapshots into it during play.
findings.caller: application advance owner.c:959 -> qa_modes_frame -> core.c:1066 mode_objects_frame -> objects.c:887 mode_ball_frame -> DeathBall respawn acquire. modes_create reserves players_order/observations but never snapshot_frames. Q1 explosion -> q1_snapshot_actors -> acquire, and Q2 radius damage -> q2_nearby -> qa_builtin_nearby also use the private pool. New nesting depth runs calloc plus malloc; nearby captures the common world snapshot then copies it to private storage.
findings.replacement: qa_world_actor_snapshot / qa_world_snapshot_capture / qa_world_radius_snapshot_capture (world.h:325-358) backed by the existing load-sized common qa_pool; use caller-owned load-prepared common pool storage for special roster snapshots and delete the growable builtin frame allocator.
findings.semantics: Keep source-edict order where requested, exact radius origin/center inclusion, current actor generation checks, nonsolid inclusion rules and nested callback lifetimes. A captured set must remain stable if damage callbacks release or spawn actors.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

partial_followups.verification: Q1 native radius, Hipnotic reversed scan and Q2 builtin nearby capture into the existing active caller buffer via the shared borrowed-storage radius API. Intermediate copies/world leases are deleted. Source order, second scratch plane, nested frames and callback cleanup are retained. Private builtin heap-backed reservation and persistent roster lifetimes remain open.

findings.summary: Active gameplay operation hooks allocate execution records on the first invocation and at each newly reached nesting depth.
findings.caller: Native damage -> qa_combat_apply -> dispatch_damage -> qa_operation_dispatch; supply/weapon inventory give or consume -> inventory dispatch -> qa_operation_dispatch. QC declared hooks (guest_qc_declared.c:262), native Q2 callbacks (:2111) and Q3 mod callbacks register active hooks. Stock no-hook direct calls do not allocate; the active-hook branch has no load-prepared frames.
findings.replacement: Common qa_pool / qa_arena storage reserved at operation or loaded-mod admission, with reusable request payloads per admitted nesting slot; delete operation_frame calloc/malloc fallback.
findings.semantics: Retain deterministic hook order, next_sequence cutoff, exactly one replacement continuation, memmove-safe changed requests, callback retirement and nested invocation lifetime.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Live pickup/equipment inventory admission creates and frees a heap transaction record instead of using the common pool.
findings.caller: application touch services.c:1370 -> qa_modes_touch -> mode_flag_touch flags.c:233 -> mode_object_count -> qa_inventory_prepare_entries when the player first carries that scoped item. Equipment respawn/configuration also calls admission_prepare -> prepare_entries. Each admission call calloc/free occurs during the gameplay operation, despite count-entry bytes themselves already using qa_pool.
findings.replacement: Use the inventory owner common qa_pool/qa_arena for bounded admission records and flexible entries, prepared during map/role configuration; retire the lease after commit/abort rather than freeing heap storage.
findings.semantics: Preserve store references held across callbacks, exact original counter policy, validation/commit atomicity and nested admissions. Do not merge game-specific count arithmetic.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: The canonical inventory still heap-allocates its per-actor store for actors spawned during play.
findings.caller: Hipnotic spawner think maps/hipnotic_spawn.c:110 and gremlin duplication gremlin.c:146 -> qa_q1_game_clone -> clone.c:167 qa_inventory_create_actor. q1_gremlin_spawn also calls create_actor. The service has an actor-capacity pointer table prepared at load, but each live new actor store uses calloc and eventual actor retirement uses free.

findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Delayed mode item publication rebuilds and heap-copies an immutable item catalog during gameplay.
findings.caller: CTF/ThreeWave startup schedules relic_spawn_ns at map.c:377. Later application advance -> qa_modes_frame -> objects.c:868 mode_relic_spawn_all -> map.c:424 qa_modes_publish_items. Publication allocates actor_capacity definitions, walks all objects and replaces each player group using calloc group/items and malloc labels. First scoped mode identity construction can also realloc and malloc.

findings.semantics: Keep mode slot/generation namespacing, concurrent modes, per-player membership, action flags and old catalog leases across callbacks. Delayed original relic spawn timing stays unchanged; only its storage/publication machinery moves.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Inventory frame publication repeatedly scans item identities and revalidates whole source groups instead of using retained item indexes.
findings.caller: Unified local/network frame -> application_unified_output_inventory unified_output.c:411/414 -> qa_inventory_entries. Each active source group calls group_validate, which calls find_in once per definition; find_in scans every source entry through callbacks. Supply and weapon give/consume/read additionally repeat local_index/group_for/definition_lookup scans by canonical item id.
findings.replacement: Load/bind/reconfigure retained qa_id_index mappings from item id plus owner to source group and source entry ordinal; validate uniqueness once at admission/revision change and read only the current authoritative value through the bound callback.
findings.semantics: Never cache mutable source counts as a duplicate store. Keep native-backed live values, definition-only versus actual-storage precedence, per-owner aliases, actor/store revisions and callback retirement detection.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: Every newly spawned pickup observer allocates a heap owner record and frees it on retirement.
findings.caller: Q1 monster death -> q1_drop_backpack -> construct_backpack -> q1_link runtime.c:1007 -> q1_pickup_observe -> qa_pickups_observe. Q2 dynamically dropped items call q2_item_change_collision -> q2_item_observe; native Q3 item admission also observes through this same service. The observation slot table grows only once, but the owner malloc happens on every admission and sweep frees retired owners.
findings.replacement: Prepare the actor-capacity observation table at qa_pickups_create and lease observer owner records from the common qa_pool; release pool slots only after calls drain, deleting per-observer malloc/free.
findings.semantics: Keep one authoritative observer per actor generation/owner, serial leases, safe replacement during an active inspection callback, retired-list lifetime and pure preview behavior.

findings.semantics: Retain name restrictions, stock baseq3/missionpack denial, mandatory pure PK3 checksums, source eight-block/2048-byte/EOF and short wire block numbering, rate and1s resend policy, offer commit/ack ordering and mount replacement semantics. findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

Retain the actual BotMemory API and one Source heap/hunk implementation as adapter policy; owner and generation remain caller-domain state, as the common pool contract requires. Common pool extension must remain explicit Source allocation/restore work, with no invented fixed Source heap limit.
findings.semantics: Source backing itself is genuine heap/hunk ABI behavior and is not the finding. Keep its four-byte HEAP_ID/HUNK_ID prefix, requested signed32-compatible sizes, zeroing and host allocation callbacks, FreeMemory hunk behavior, allocation insertion/report order, generation changes on slot reuse, same-owner checkpoint preservation of surviving backing/handles, fresh recreated generations and cold save ordinal references. Slot metadata migration must preserve the current smallest-initial-slot/LIFO-reuse behavior and arbitrary checkpoint survivor slots, with no competing allocator or actor-only index substituted for nonactor identities.

findings.summary: QW retains a separate binary64 coordinate vector that the original QW mover does not have, and propagates that representation through Unified frames.
findings.caller: The QuakeWorld QC control adapter builds qa_qw_movement_state.origin by widening the authored origin before adding mins. The common control path invokes qa_movement_move at control.c:2860 and selects the QW mover; a stationary spectator returns at quakeworld.c:282 without any float vector store, retaining that wider origin. The QC projection later casts back through control_word, and Unified frame layout stores all three coordinates as F64. This is an engine state representation, not a required legacy wire width.
findings.replacement: Use qa_vec3 for the authoritative QW origin, storing the original centered expression once at the QC/module adapter, and use common vector operations with original QW evaluation/storage semantics. Remove qa_qw_origin, its projection helpers and the retained-binary64 numeric flag/layout.
findings.semantics: Original reference read: qsrc/quake/QW/client/mathlib.h:22-23 defines vec3_t as float[3]; pmove.h:54 uses vec3_t origin; QW/server/sv_user.c:1428-1429 stores origin + (mins - player_mins) into that float vector before Pmove. Current guest_qc.c:703-705 instead evaluates (double)origin + mins + constant without the original grouping or float store. Preserve original float stores, expression grouping, spectator early return, original protocol coordinate widths and all other QW rule tails. Source confirms a representation/rounding difference; no live symptom or timing is asserted.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof

findings.summary: The common physical-input path still grows held-input and per-action source arrays during key dispatch.
findings.caller: frontend frame.c:500 dispatches a queued qa_sys_event to qa_input_platform_dispatch; translated physical presses reach qa_input_seat_event, digital and run_binding. digital calls qa_input_reserve for each new held source when its retained capacity is insufficient (seat.c:588). An action binding then calls qa_input_seat_action -> qa_input_button_down, which reallocates on the fifth simultaneous distinct source for one action, and again at later capacity boundaries. Console +button commands reach the same action API through bindings.c:92.
findings.replacement: Reserve held/source storage from admitted bindings and device/control capacities during load/bind, using the common arena or pool ownership primitive, and reuse it during dispatch. Keep one button implementation; do not replace growth with an arbitrary source-dropping cap.
findings.semantics: This is capacity-triggered allocation, not allocation on every frame or every key press. Preserve multiple simultaneous bindings/devices to one action, duplicate/OS-repeat suppression, reference-held old bindings during rebinding, partial source release, release events during UI/focus handoff, and held-time fractions. The existing event queue itself is used; the bypass is downstream live storage growth.
findings.verification: source review; no runtime or performance proof
